#3720. Remember PS5-exclusive shooter Fairgame$? It’s reportedly canceled now, to no one’s surprise

Well, it seems like this one was only a matter of time.

Sony has reportedly canceled the long-missing online shooter Fairgame$ after it went missing in the public eye for years, according to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, adding to a long list of canceled PlayStation projects this generation.

Schreier said that “a recent test of the game with thousands of players did not deliver on the results PlayStation expected,” according to an internal email sent to employees today.

First revealed at PlayStation Showcase way back in May 2023, the game seemed to be themed around online heist PvP gameplay. But it hasn’t been seen since, and this cancellation comes as little surprise, as rumors about turmoil in development have been swirling for some time.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the memo. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

Earlier this year, it was reported that Fairgame$ was pivoting away from the “heist” mechanic and instead focusing on the extraction game type, similar to Bungie’s Marathon and Call of Duty’s DMZ. It apparently did not work out.

Fairgame$, developed by Haven Studios, joins a long list of PS5 projects that did not make the cut this generation as Sony incessantly chased live-service success. Concord launched and was quickly shuttered, while The Last of Us Factions, a God of War game, a Spider-Man game, Twisted Metal, and more never saw the light of day from PS5’s games-as-a-service initiative.

According to Schreier, “there will be no job cuts as a result of the cancellation,” and “Haven will instead move to support other studios within the organization.”

Reflector Entertainment had a new game in pre-production, but Bandai decided it wasn't worth the time or money to pursue.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Two years after the release of Unknown 9: Awakening, its one and only game, Bandai Namco's Reflector Entertainment is closing.

The shutdown was revealed in a notice posted by Banda Namco (via Game Informer) saying the company "has passed a resolution to dissolve and liquidate its consolidated subsidiary Reflector Entertainment." The decision was made "after comprehensively considering future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation," Bandai Namco said.

Unknown 9: Awakening, featuring The Witcher star Anya Chalotra as a woman able to travel into a mysterious dimension known as the Fold, showed potential in our pre-release preview as a "linear, narrative-driven, set-piece laden" game drawing from Xbox 360 releases of the late 2000s.

The full game, however, landed with a thud. A month after launch, Reflector laid off 18% of its workforce; a few months after that, in January 2025, more layoffs followed as an in-development project was cancelled. Reflector CEO Herve Hoerdt said at the time that the decision "correlates directly with the failure of the studio's ambitious and courageous first project [Unknown 9: Awakening]," which "didn't come near the company expectations."

Reflector confirmed the coming end of operations in its own message on LinkedIn, writing that "after reviewing the progress of our latest project in pre-production, future development requirements, and current market conditions, Bandai Namco concluded that it could not justify several more years of investment."

Bandai Namco said the liquidation of Reflector Entertainment is expected to happen "once the necessary procedures according to local laws are completed," but a concrete schedule has not been set.

#3718. As Arc Raiders celebrates its first birthday, publisher Nexon reveals the extraction shooter has topped 17 million sales, but revenue is set to decline

Arc Raiders, Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter, has exceeded 17m copies sold, according to publisher Nexon.

Arc Raiders was released at the end of October 2025, so reaching that milestone in a year is nothing to scoff at. According to Nexon's latest earnings report, however, only 1m copies of those 17 were sold in the third quarter - meaning sales have certainly slowed down.

Relatedly, Nexon said it expects Arc Raiders' revenue to decline in the fourth quarter compared to the same period last year - when the game enjoyed its hugely successful launch - and anticipates revenue will be "broadly flat sequentially". Despite this, the company said Arc Raiders' revenue was "within the outlook", naming its Frozen Trail update as a key moment that brought back some lapsed players while introducing new ones.

Indeed, Frozen Trail boosted the game's Steam player count, and reports suggest it also helped Arc Raiders hit a six-month player high across various platforms.

Even with its slowing sales, Arc Raiders remains one of Nexon's most successful titles. The company primarily attributed an overall year-on-year revenue increase, for the nine months ended 30th September, to the game.

Looking ahead, the biggest question hanging over Arc Raiders is whether or not it's going to get a dedicated PvE playlist. Following a successful test earlier this summer, Embark has been coy, and hasn't said whether PvE will return as a permanent feature. Arc Raiders' Chinese version does have a dedicated PvE mode, and executive producer Aleksander Grøndal said he could see both PvP and PvE modes co-existing in the future.

Now that the snowman is built, he needs his own mode of transportation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We can all agree that the Olaf animatronic walking itself around Disneyland Paris is adorable, all on its own. Now it's even cuter, with his own magical sleigh to help transport him around the Kingdom of Arendelle as he makes his way to a stage where the Arendelle Carolers perform for the holidays.

One of the biggest drawbacks that came with introducing a “living” animatronic Olaf to guests in Disney’s European theme park is the fact that it can’t walk very far very quickly. I mean, he is a snowman after all. So now, and just in time for the holiday celebration, the adorable snowman who just wants to live his best summer is taking on winter in style with his own magical sleigh. Check out the short clip of a cast member steering Olaf around as he waves to the adoring masses gathered around:

A post shared by EveryCharacter.com (@everycharacter)

The holidays are in full swing in the Disney theme parks around the world, and no one embodies the winter season better than Olaf the snowman from Frozen, one of Walt Disney Animation Studios’ most popular franchises of all time. As a result, I’m happy to see that the beloved character has his own mode of transportation, especially after a few incidents of Olaf failing, freezing, and falling over. It’s a frightening sight when it happens, though Josh Gad has kept a sense of humor about it all, as the actor who is responsible for the snowman's lovable personality.

Getting to meet beloved Disney characters is a longtime tradition, where animated characters become live-action characters in the parks. While we knew that Disney Parks had been working on robots for a few years, it wasn’t until we actually got to see Olaf in action that I realized just how remarkable the achievement was. I’m also thankful that they’re continuing to build on that by creating this sleigh, which seems to have a purpose bigger than just transporting the character around the World of Frozen in Disneyland Paris.

In the video clip, you can see that Olaf’s sleigh, while too freaking cute just on its own, has the dual purpose of also working as a bridge to get him onto the stage at the foot of North Mountain so that he can join the Arendelle carolers for a 15-minute musical performance where he leads the choir. The sleigh transforms into a short platform that Olaf can shuffle across to the back of the stage where he can do his part in the show, avoiding the need for someone to have to physically lift him up and get him on the stage some other way.

While more Frozen films are in the works, we won’t see Frozen 3 until November 24, 2027. Until then, I’m hoping we’ll get more Olaf fun in and around the Disney theme parks, as he’s a character that would be a welcome addition to the U.S. locations as well.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the WildThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of TimeThe Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

My friends, put the tomatoes down. I havenât even gotten to speak yet. I, like most people who own a Nintendo Switch 2 and are killing time until Grand Theft Auto 6 launches next week, am playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Iâm having a pretty good time going back to a game that was once an elementary school obsession for me, especially because itâs been a long time since I really felt a constant sense of progression in a Zelda game after a decade of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

Yeah, the game is incredibly simple by modern standards, and Nintendo has done a lot to ensure that by making the game demonstrably easier in dozens of small ways that add up, but I think that relative simplicity is what draws me to it. Iâve been chipping away at the game in short sessions, usually finishing a temple or two before putting it down for the rest of the day, and the tangible feeling of momentum is what keeps me coming back to it just about every other evening at this point.

Over the years, especially with the rise of open-world games, I have identified that I am a goal-oriented person when it comes to how a video game can hold my attention. Thereâs just so much competition for whatever spare hours I have that if the bulk of my time playing a game is spent getting to the things I care about, I can lose interest fairly quickly. I want to see where the story goes, I want to reach the end of a quest line, and I loathe tedious open-world traversal more than most video game activities.Â

I canât entirely avoid open-world games in 2026, but if a game doesnât have a quick or engaging way to get around a giant map, it actively deters me from playing it. I often cite the Infamous series, with all its superpowered movement and interesting environmental interactions, as a great example of a game that makes its open-world map tolerable to me. A car or a horse is probably not going to cut it. There are exceptions from time to time, such as Cyberpunk 2077âs Night City entrancing me so much that Iâd gladly take in the view as I drove around on my motorcycle. But if I can help it, I want to spend my limited gaming time on things that arenât simply moving from one side of a giant space to another.

Breath of the Wild and its excellent sequel, Tears of the Kingdom do a lot to break up the tedium of simply moving through a space. The survival sim-esque friction and gizmo-building mechanics are brilliant evolutions of the original Zelda formula, and Nintendoâs ability to still draw water from the well of a decades-old franchise is commendable. I really enjoyed my time with both games, despite them grinding against a lot of my ingrained gaming sensibilities. The puzzles in the shrines, the constant feeling of discovery in its giant open world, and the colorful casts of weirdos and heroes you meet throughout the games maintain all that same Zelda spirit, but with a meaningful expansion of what a Zelda game looks like.Â

But man, is it a relief to go back to Ocarina of Time. I want puzzle-solving and discovery that I can get to quickly, that doesnât need me to meaningfully prep a survival bag so I can trek to the other side of the map while hoping my melee weapons can last me the whole trip, and what Ocarina is delivering feels downright breezy. Iâm sorry, Iâm sorry. I know itâs regressive of me to say Iâd like for the series to strip away all the cool things itâs done in the past nine years, but I havenât had a Zelda experience that feels like this in so long. The top-down 2D games are similar (at least those that came after the pretty open-ended and opaque original game), but they donât have the targeting and swordplay of the postâOcarina of Time era that rounds out the vision I have of what makes a 3D Zelda game.

I donât really hold any illusions that Zelda is going to go back to the structure of Ocarina of Time, but it is refreshing to be handed the tools I need to accomplish things without worrying that my weapon is going to break from battle damage or that Iâll run out of some vital consumable before I reach my goal. The Legend of Zelda is gonna be fine no matter where it goes moving forward, but for as dated and small in scope as Ocarina of Time might feel compared to Tears of the Kingdom, it sure does remind me that there was once a time when I didnât feel like I was fighting against the elements just to get to where I wanted to go.

#3715. How to gain more Followers in Warhammer Survivors

Gaining Followers in Warhammer Survivors has many benefits when it comes to the survival aspect of the game. Not only do they help you survive and last longer in the battle, but you’ll need to gain a minimum number if you want to complete the objectives.

While this method talks about gaining 5 followers, it can be any arbitrary number. I say 5 because that’s a requirement of an in-game objective that unlocks a crucial item. There is more than one way to gain followers, but this will be the easiest one for you.

First, unlock Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski and Sister Superior Amalia Novena, followed by their respective weapons. Now, begin a fresh run with Malum Caedo.

Once you’re deeper into your run, you’ll be offered the Lasgun and Shield of Faith as available weapons. Grab both of them, and then upgrade the Lasgun to Level 6. This will make Bartosz Kozlowski bring the required number of followers.

If you’re one short, that’s where Sister Amalia comes in. Once you acquire the Shield of Faith as a weapon, you’ll manage to have her as a companion. This will also unlock the Figure Case passive skill that allows you to return after dying.

You can repeat the same process with other characters in the game. Several characters allow you to add to the count of Followers when you unlock their signature weapon and level it up. However, the characters I have mentioned above are easy to unlock, and they will allow you to get to five Followers fast.

#3714. Steam now shows average Steam Deck framerates when browsing games, but Valve says it's considering expanding the feature to other hardware

By providing average data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture".

Valve has released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

As per Valve's announcement post, average framerates are now listed in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of a game's store page, but you'll need to click Learn More to see it. Additionally, the feature is only available for games that have been tested for Deck compatibility - those with Verified, Playable, or Unsupported badges - so while it's not a complete list, it still covers thousands of titles.

According to Valve, average framerates are derived from players running the game on their Steam Decks, assuming they've opted in to provide framerate data. And the store widget also includes another helpful addition: a histogram displaying the percentage of data samples. This shows how often a particular framerate has been reported, and is useful in determining if the game's framerate is sporadic, such as due to stutters.

"The current Steam Deck Verified compatibility rating is based on standardised test criteria, but it may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay," Valve explained of the new feature.

"This is especially true around performance - a game with an Unsupported rating due to unstable performance may be considered playable by some customers, and a Verified game may not reach a framerate that some customers prefer to play at. By providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions."

Currently, Steam's framerate data feature only covers performance on Steam Deck, and for a very good reason: Valve's handheld has standardised hardware, so the results will be the same for all players. However, Valve says it intends to provide framerate data for more devices in the future, but it's not clear if that's ever going to include desktop PCs, considering the complex nature of their hardware configurations.

The Symbiosis update, which will also kick off a beta for a new Team Deathmatch mode, will launch on December 8 with a free-play week.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Bungie has served up our first proper look at Marathon's big Symbiosis update, which is set to go live on December 8 with a permanent PvE mode, plus an all-new Team Deathmatch mode and a social space called Limbo.

Symbiosis represents the start of "the evolution of Marathon," Bungie said, with "a plethora of updates and changes" to the game. First and foremost is the addition of Marathon's PvE mode, now permanent and with a new name, Expedition, that's described in the teaser as a "co-op PvE roguelite." Details beyond that haven't been revealed just yet, but Bungie called it "phase one" of the team's PvE plan, suggesting that it remains a work in progress.

Also notable in Symbiosis is the addition of Limbo, a "social space" where players can hang out without getting aired out (although there does appear to be a little area set aside for friendly shootin'), and its firing range, a handy way to test the game's guns without having to venture into its less friendly locales.

Speaking of which, the Perimeter map is being expanded with new points of interest and tunnels, and a new sword-wielding runner shell, Bishop, will debut with the update. For those who prefer the PvP life, the update will also kick off a beta for Marathon's Team Deathmatch mode.

Overall, Symbiosis looks to be a pretty big deal, and while today's tease is light on detail, the early reaction among players on Reddit and social media seems quite positive. Bishop is already racking up fans:

One other bit of good news: The rollout of Symbiosis on December 8 will also mark the start of an "open play week," during which the game will be fully free to play, including the new modes and content. If you dig it and decide to stick around (ie., buy the game), any progress and items earned will carry over.

#3712. How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR, all lockpick types, and how to use them

Although brute force can take you far in DREADMOOR, having a lockpick at hand is a requirement if you wish to get past locked doors and access treasure chests across the game’s many settlements.

But getting the tool means first acquiring its recipe, something only doable a few hours in. Here’s how to get the first lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR and how the mechanic works.

You can unlock the Crude Lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR as a reward by completing the Catch a Mutant Fish Story Quest. The quest is unlocked after meeting Mad Nick on his island and requires catching two Cryptmaw fish.

The fish can be found in the locations below, but only late at night. You will also need to have at least 30 Line Strength to attempt the catch, so don’t forget to equip the Braided Line to your fishing rod at the trading post to meet the requirements.

After returning to Mad Nick and unlocking the recipe, you will be able to craft the Crude Lockpick by using 1x Rubber and 1x Metal Plate. You can have a maximum of twelve in your inventory. Just don’t forget, they will share slots with First Aid Kits.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

You can pick locks in DREADMOOR by first using your mouse to position your lockpick and find the sweet spot within the lock, marked by a glowing light. Now, hold D to turn the lock while keeping the tool in the right position to unlock it. Forcing the lock will cause your lockpick to break.

Apart from the Crude Lockpick, you can unlock two other variants in DREADMOOR: the standard iron Lockpick and the Master Lockpick. Both are clear upgrades and can be crafted after unlocking their respective recipes.

We will be adding more to the above once we unlock the recipes for the advanced lockpicks. In the meantime, don’t forget to check out all Fishing Rods and how they work in DREADMOOR.

#3711. Rockstar kills any hopes of streaming GTA 6 from Xbox to PC, but you can stream it to your old Xbox One if you like

Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S. And as part of the same announcement, the developer revealed a key detail about the game's cloud streaming options.

GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming. However, this is only possible on Xbox Series X/S consoles, as well as - surprisingly - the last generation console, Xbox One. Notably, that means you can't use Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream to PC, or other devices, despite it being useable there.

You may recall that in early October, a Verge report said Microsoft had acquired exclusive cloud streaming rights for GTA 6, with the understanding being that the game would be available to stream on any XCloud-supported device - as in, to PC as well. Xbox immediately shot down the report, saying GTA 6 "will not be streaming exclusively or to PC".

Perhaps more surprisingly, the cloud-streamed version will be using Series S graphics settings, not those of the more powerful Series X console. Considering the loss in quality inherent in cloud streaming, this will make for a less-than-ideal way of experiencing the game.

Beyond cloud streaming, GTA 6 supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox, so you can stream the game on your local network to any device, from a PS5 or Xbox Series X/S console.

GTA 6 pre-loading is now available across PlayStation and Xbox. The code-in-box physical editions have also started shipping, letting you claim the code and pre-load your copy in time for GTA 6's 19th November launch.

Another one of PlayStation’s live-service games has crashed and burned, asÂ Fairgames, the company’s online shooter that was being developed by first-party PlayStation developer Haven Studios, has been canceled.

As reported by Bloomberg, Haven Studios isn’t undergoing any layoffs as a result of the cancelation, as “the studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities,” according to a statement provided to the publication by PlayStation. The decision comes after Fairgames‘ recent playtest didn’t live up to Sony’s internal expectations.

âWhile the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,â PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees and verified by Bloomberg. âCombined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.â

FairgamesÂ was initially announced back in 2023, and was originally being led by Jade Raymond, known as a producer of the earlyÂ Assassin’s Creed games. Raymond left Haven Studios in 2025, though the project quietly continued development. We really haven’t heard much about the game since it was initially unveiled.

Haven Studios was initially founded in 2021, and Sony acquired the company in 2022 before it had even put out a game. Now, it sounds like those who had been working onÂ FairgamesÂ will support the development of other games by PlayStation studios.

Fairgames is the latest in a long line of live-service disasters for Sony as the company continues to greenlight and then cancel its various attempts at forever games. Perhaps most famously, the company removed multiplayer shooter Concord from storefronts and then subsequently shut down its developer, Firewalk Studios.

Despite all this, Sony is still adamant that live-service games are an important part of PlayStation’s future.

An era in superhero-related media is officially coming to an end, as James Gunn and Peter Safran are officially stepping down from their posts as the co-CEOs of DC Studios. This surprising news arrives only a few weeks after the finalization of the Paramount/Warner Bros. merger. At this point, the news is still very fresh and, based on social media, the responses to this major development vary tremendously. Interestingly enough, amid all that, one fan brought up a wild fact regarding Gunn’s tenure, and I’m feeling so many emotions.

Gunn and Safran joined DC Studios in 2022 and, from there, they began to construct their DCU continuity, which was to span movies, TV and video games. The pair eventually developed a ten-year plan and, up to this point, that strategy has yielded films like Superman and Supergirl as well as shows like Creature Commandos and Lanterns. The wild comment that was recently shared by an X user had nothing to do with any projects like that, though. Instead, they marked the end of this chapter by naming a long-gestating flick:

Very funny/sad that the entire Gunn era took place between THE BATMAN and THE BATMAN PART 2.

I’m honestly at a loss for words here, as this fact is absolutely correct. Matt Reeves’ The Batman was released in March 2022 months before Safran and Gunn were hired. The sequel was announced in April of that year and, since then, the movie has seen a variety of delays and is currently set to hit theaters in early 2028. On the one hand, it’s understandable that someone would chuckle over the fact that this sequel’s development will have outlasted the Gunn/Safran era. But, on the other hand, I’m actually a bit sad.

James Gunn Doesn’t Hold Back About Rumors Swirling Around Man Of Tomorrow And More DC Projects

As someone who has been interested in the DCU thus far, I’m a bit disappointed over the possibility of another reboot. However, what really makes me sad about the fact pointed out in the social media is that it’s a reminder of just how long The Batman: Part II’s development has taken. Of course, I do understand the reasons, though, as the Hollywood strikes played a key role in that. Also, more recently, Reeves had to take a step back from the film to handle a personal matter, and Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to complete principal photography. Reeves isn’t leaving the movie entirely, though, as he'll remain in touch with Soderbergh during the shoot and completely retake the reins during post-production.

It was just weeks ago that Reeves’ situation was announced and it was mentioned that he had support from Safran and Gunn. That’s just one detail that makes the news of their departure all the more surreal to me. Gunn posted about his exit on his Instagram and reflected on the highs of working for DC. Additionally, the filmmaker praised the various collaborators he had the chance to work with. Overall, Gunn – a longtime fan of DC Comics – seems to have a lot of gratitude for his time serving as co-CEO of the studio.

While James Gunn and Peter Safran will vacate their positions ahead of Jeremy Latcham’s arrival by December 1, their work within the DCU isn’t done just yet as, at the very least, he’s still in post-production on his Superman follow-up, Man of Tomorrow, which is set to be released amid the 2027 movie schedule. Also, Gunn and Safran are still credited as producers on The Batman’s sequel. I’m not sure what lies ahead for DC but, for now, I’m going to be glued to my screen to see if any other fans drop any other wild facts.

Man of Tomorrow soars into theaters on July 9, 2027, while The Batman: Part II opens on February 18, 2028.

#3708. I think China just taught a lesson about AI that US audiences really should learn

And I'm not talking about Nvidia-related spycraft.

One of the wildest entertainment stories of the year was Niu Lai, a Chinese animated film that immediately became a laughing stock for its incredibly rudimentary animation and character models.

And even though taste is in the eye of the beholder, I find it very hard to believe anyone would like this at face value. “Why is something that looks worse than many Newgrounds animations from the early ’00s even showing in theaters?” You might ask, but it turns out Niu Lai was a family’s labor of love that lucked into a modest distribution. This crucial piece of information turned the tide and got people to see the film in droves, giving it a $9 million theatrical run on a pretty much non-existent budget.

And while one could argue that a lot of people only started to care about the film because they learned the story about its creation, well, that’s completely fair, because film is a vessel for connection.

Niu Lai‘s story becomes even more interesting when you realize China recently saw the release of Sanxingdui: Future Past, the country’s first fully AI movie release, which bombed hard. Sure, it could perhaps make a comeback, but it can’t count on its development tale to pull the heartstrings of moviegoers because its production, like any other AI production, amounts to that of a bunch of guys using a computer to type the plot of the movie they wanted to rip off.

A studio spent $1.5 million on the first-ever theatrical AI film, which ended up grossing 100.000 dollars. A very different outcome from that of the millions of LinkedIn users who claim to have only spent $100 on a Lord of the Rings ripoff too ludicrous to even imagine.

Westerners with only one photo in their profile and no background to speak of often claim China’s population shows way more openness to the prospects of an AI-led future than the people of the West, but that might, fortunately, be bunk.

Unfortunately, however, the theatrical run of Wildwood shows that the West might’ve become too desensitized even for the most amazing displays of true animation prowess of all time. Yes, despite being arguably the most impressive animated film I’ve ever witnessed, and also being the result of many intense years of loving work, Laika’s epic also failed to even recoup its budget. Honestly, I’d normally advise you against seeing the trailer, but if that’s what’ll earn it a few more ticket sales, then so be it:

On top of being as far from using AI as a movie can get, Wildwood is also the best-rated animated movie in a decade. As far as technique and spectacle go, it’s perfectly reasonable to call this the Avatar or even the Star Wars of stop-motion movies—and a work capable of going toe to toe with any live-action or traditional ( or CGI) animated film, but people just didn’t care, or didn’t know.

Yeah, the marketing team either didn’t have the resources, or didn’t do a great job. Still, the stellar reactions to Wildwood should’ve at least granted it a healthy word-of-mouth-fed growth, but it’s yet to pass the $70 million mark worldwide, a number that stops very short of the movie’s budget—and truth is, the real budget has never even been officially revealed, but that can only mean it’s that big. And, if you’ve seen the movie, you’ll know there’s no way Laika studio pulled this off with the $100 million budget that some people were floating around.

It’s great to see Niu Lai succeed while an AI-made film crashes and burns, but it’d have been even better if that beautiful event had also sent shockwaves that got people to watch more beautifully crafted stuff, because we might never get to see anything like Wildwood again. Even if that means we might also not be seeing many more AI-made movies, either.

#3707. Europe is about to get very tough on loot boxes in games, according to a leaked draft of the landmark Digital Fairness Act

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences..."

An alleged draft of the potentially game-changing Digital Fairness Act has leaked ahead of its scheduled publication tomorrow (11th November), containing proposals that could dramatically affect the way games operate and are monetised within the European Union.

The draft, published by French publication Contexte (via Video Games Industry Memo) goes as far as to recommend that loot boxes (uncertainty-based rewards) be turned off by default for minors, as well as the sale of in-game items and currencies. There's also a recommendation that all players - not just minors - should be able to turn off offers related to these lootboxes and gambling mechanics.

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences," the draft of the Digital Fairness Act begins. "It has enabled faster, more convenient and wider access to an ever-increasing range of goods and services. At the same time, it has given rise to new and more sophisticated ways of influencing consumers' choices.

"Along with the indisputable benefits in choice and efficiency, the extensive use of digital technologies allows both old and new unfair commercial practices to affect consumers at scale, exacerbating risks to their economic interests, as well as to their mental and physical wellbeing. Vulnerable consumers are particularly affected."

The Digital Fairness Act calls for greater transparency around a "transactional decision". Which means: "Price transparency on the real value of in-app purchases using virtual currencies and the probabilities of winning for virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards (loot boxes).

"All consumers can turn off virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards. Some spending-maximising practices prohibited for minors, with the remaining turned off by default. Supporting self-regulation for video games and legal obligation for video games to have an age-appropriate rating. All consumers can turn off attention-maximising features, with some prohibited for minors and the remaining turned off by default."

"Spending-maximising" refers to systems that pressure us to spend more money than we want to, such as reward systems or pay-to-progress or pay-to-win systems. They're all being targeted here, as is virtual currency, which provides a layer of abstraction as to the real cost of goods.

"It may be difficult for minors to resist such perceived pressure to pay," the Digital Fairness Act said with regard to progression-linked systems. "Therefore, where a product is directed at minors or when the trader is aware with reasonable certainty that the product is used by minors, pay-to-progress or pay-to-win mechanisms [...] should not be made available to minors."

The Digital Fairness Act is a forthcoming European legislative proposal designed to update consumer protection rules for various digital dangers that we face today. Importantly, it's not law yet, and it has iterations and discussions to go through before it will be. A timeline on the Digital Fairness Act explainer website suggests it could be adopted late in 2027, then applied more broadly by 2030.

It's also hoping to tackle many things besides shady video game monetisation, including "problematic" influencer marketing, "unfair" pricing practices - such as obscuring the real cost of something until you've progressed through layers trying to buy it - and mysterious-sounding "dark patterns". These relate to 'easy to sign-up, hard-to-cancel' processes, it seems.

These changes aren't happening in a vacuum. Earlier this year, the well-known European age-rating body PEGI announced historic alterations to its game-rating criteria, with an eye to better categorising the dangers of loot box-containing games and aggressively monetised games. These changes have already started to roll out and mean that a game like EA Sports FC, which was previously routinely rated PEGI 3, now automatically gets a PEGI 16 rating because of its Ultimate Team card pack (loot box) system.

The effect of the Digital Fairness Act could tip the balance against these systems being included in games at all. Expect more discussion and digestion of the proposed changes as the Act is officially published tomorrow.

Capcom still hasn't announced a release date for Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, the Sunbreak-scale DLC that was revealed in February, but it seems like we might be getting a chance to sample the expansion before too long. A recent Steam listing update has provided a strong reason to suspect that there'll be a public beta for Ascendance available ahead of its launch in 2027.

As SteamDB changelogs show, the Steam app entry for Monster Hunter Wilds' 2024 public beta was quietly updated early this morning to change the app's name from "Monster Hunter Wilds Beta test" to "Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test." Similarly, the listing's visual assets were updated to feature key art of a hunter facing an Arateka, one of the new monsters being introduced in the expansion.

And sure enough, while the Wilds beta was removed from player libraries after it ended, it's possible for users who'd previously played it to confirm its listing changes within the Steam app by viewing their own played games from their Steam profile. I just looked. It says Ascendance right there.

As the previous Wilds beta consisted of a repackaged demo build, it's likely that an Ascendance beta would follow suit: I'd expect a similar set of hunts to what in-person attendees were able to get hands-on time with at Tokyo Game Show in September, offering a chance to try out the new Boost Bracer weapon mechanics in Master Rank combat.

If a beta does materialize, it'll hopefully be a smoother experience than what beta hunters got in 2024. The early Wilds playtest was the first time PC players encountered the dreaded origami monsters, a symptom of the severe optimization issues that tanked Wilds' reputation for over a year after launch.

As for when that beta might be available, we can only speculate—but given that Monster Hunter has made prior appearances at Geoff Keighley productions, a public playtest that accompanies a hypothetical Game Awards trailer makes intuitive sense. But I'm just reading the tea leaves here—Capcom hasn't said a word about when it'll offer its next DLC teaser.

#3705. Rockstar details Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Pro enhancements, but it'll still only run at 30FPS

Pushing consoles to "their absolute limits".

As Grand Theft Auto 6 preloads go live, developer Rockstar has detailed the enhancements coming to the PS5 Pro version of the game, confirming these won't include framerates above the 30 FPS its targeting for consoles.

Rockstar shared the news in a blog post released to announce that GTA 6 pre-loading is now available ahead of its release date on 19th November.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles," Rockstar says. It goes on to reconfirm GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on all consoles, saying the game is pushing modern machines "to their absolute limits" in order to "bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

PS5 players can expect high-fidelity haptic feedback through the DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio, and Tempest 3D audio, while PS5 Pro enhancements come in the form of PSSR support and ray tracing shadows, which should make the game look especially fancy, plus improved load times. PlayStation players can also expect remote play support. As for the Xbox, the post clarified details on Xbox Cloud Gaming, which will allow the game to be streamed to Xbox consoles including the Xbox One. Notably, this won't work on PC.

Grand Theft Auto 6's 30 FPS target was previously confirmed by Rockstar back in August, but there was some uncertainty around a possible 60fps performance mode at the time. Still, those PS5 technical boons do a lot of work to improve the games it's applied to, which if nothing else should mean GTA 6 will be quite the looker.

#3703. You Can Play GTA 6 On A 13-Year-Old Xbox And It’ll Run At The Same Framerate As PS5 Pro

GTA 6PS5 ProXbox Cloud GamingXbox Series X/S

Grand Theft Auto 6 is only coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, but that doesn’t mean those consoles will be the only places to play it. Technically, fans who are still on Xbox One, which came out back in 2013, will also have a shot at exploring Rockstar Games’ latest version of Vice City thanks to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Microsoft revealed the surprise last-gen perk in an update to its cloud gaming program this week. “Grand Theft Auto VI will be playable on day one through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S, starting at 1am ET,” the company announced. “That means more players can experience one of the most anticipated games of the year on the consoles they already own. The game uses Xbox Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with Xbox Cloud Gaming.”

Series S graphics settings include the game running at a targeted 30fps framerate, the same as what will be available to players on Xbox Series X and PS5, as well as PS5 Pro. Sony’s more powerful hardware will still give players access to improved image quality with PSSR, but the game won’t run at 60fps anywhere, at least not at launch.

So what do you need in order to play GTA 6 on an Xbox One? Well, you’ll still need to own a digital copy of the game, which costs $80 and began pre-loading this week. You’ll also need access to Xbox Cloud Gaming, either via a Game Pass subscription or via Ã  la carte pricing. Ten hours of cloud gaming time in Vice City will cost Xbox owners $4.

What you won’t be able to do is stream GTA 6 to a mobile device or PC. Those options, which are a standard part of the rest of Xbox Cloud Gaming’s offerings, are excluded from the streaming agreement with Rockstar. It’s unclear if that’s a functionality that may be added sometime down the road after the game has been out for a while. GTA 6 will also support remote play on both Xbox and PS5, meaning you can stream it to other screens locally, including the PS Portal.

“Weâre excited to bring Grand Theft Auto 6 to more Xbox players at launch, and we will also be adding more titles from Rockstar Games to Xbox Cloud Gaming including Grand Theft Auto 5, Red Dead Redemption 2, and more in the coming months,” Microsoft added in today’s announcement.

I have no idea how many Xbox Ones are still out in the wild, or how many people may be tempted to blow the dust off of them instead of upgrading to a current-gen console. But given the ongoing price hikes for both the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, it’s a really nice option for those who can’t otherwise afford to buy new hardware this fall for GTA 6.

I can barely remember a time when Carson Daly wasn’t hosting something on my TV screen.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Carson Daly has been a host and a constant presence in my life since the ‘90s. I first became aware of him with his spot as a nighttime host on L.A.’s influential and highly rated alternative rock station KROQ-FM. So, by the time he became a presence on MTV with Total Request Live when the show debuted in 1998, he was already a trusted voice in music and pop culture for me.

Before YouTube and social media, MTV was the place to go if you wanted to be exposed to music you might not have already been aware of yet, and TRL brought heightened awareness to the pop princesses and boy bands of the era. You could catch the hottest music videos of the time while also seeing celebrities drop by to chat with Carson Daly about projects they were promoting.

He always had an ease and comfort with the talent but could also engage with the very passionate viewers as they agreed and disagreed with him. And there’s something comforting about seeing him officially step into the gig as co-host of Saturday Today, all these years later. The Voice host expressed his gratitude to People when reflecting on his latest gig:

I started many years ago at MTV and I feel like I’ve been really lucky. I’ve sort of grown up with an audience. So, if you were 18 and came to TRL, you might be 38 now and have a couple of kids and come to the Plaza. And so, I’ve just been lucky generationally to continue to work in TV, have new opportunities and people have been there with me.

While I never went to TRL in person, and likely won’t make it to the Plaza where they shoot Today, I did tune in often, especially when the likes of Britney Spears or any other popular pop stars were performing, so that I could teach myself the dance steps, to varying degrees of success. I am part of that audience that has grown up with Carson Daly, and I continue to watch him across a variety of projects to this day. And although I do miss the glimpse Total Request Live gave viewers into the lives of the biggest music stars of that era, the most recent attempt at a revival and the decline of MTV in general have made that impossible to recapture.

As someone who has had the successful host on my own TV screen over the decades, I found it particularly touching that when he officially added the Saturday Today co-anchor job in New York City to his already busy schedule that includes shooting The Voice in Los Angeles, he immediately thought of his mother watching the Today Show in their kitchen while he was getting ready for school. He clearly knows how proud his mother would have been to see her son become a part of something that was so important to her own life. Daly explained:

Well, I thought about my mom. My mom, God rest her soul, was the biggest ‘Today Show’ fan of all time. When I was growing up – elementary, junior high and high school – every morning I went in the kitchen, the ‘Today Show’ was on a tiny little TV. And when I got this job, just being here, she was here.

Admitting he teared up over how his mother would feel about his latest hosting gig made me tear up in the process, knowing firsthand how hard it is not to share such a big accomplishment with the one person you know it would mean the most to. He also joked that the other bonus of being gone on Saturday mornings is that it gets him out of making breakfast for his kids, but that they better not DoorDash as a replacement since that’s just too expensive.

There are still rumors that Carson Daly will be leaving The Voice after Season 30 wraps on the 2026 TV schedule, which likely won’t die down anytime soon, especially with Keke Palmer stepping in as host for Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity. But until we know for sure, the former TRL host can be seen doing his thing on Saturday Today as well as guiding the The Voice singers through the return of the Live Shows as they get closer to announcing a winner in December.

#3701. Main Sequence release countdown: Exact date and time

First-person space-sim factory Main Sequence is coming soon to gamers worldwide, and you won’t need to wait long to begin your adventure. Developed by the Tumbling Dumpling Studio, the game allows you to design different spaceships, build space stations, and explore the dark space.

But before we jump into our space stations, let’s find out when the game goes live.

Main Sequence goes live on Thursday, Nov. 12. The release date was announced b the publishers earlier during Steam Fest, and I am not expecting any change this late. The following countdown will expire once the game goes live.

The countdown is based on the following times.

In Main Sequence, you have been tasked with expanding humanity’s footprint among the stars. To do so, you’ll need to collect resources, expand your base of operations, and automate the production.

In the beginning, you’ll have a single mining ship, which is good enough to get the starting resources. As you do research and unlock the upgrades, you can quickly expand your base of operations to operate a fully automated factory.

When it comes to designing your ship, factories, and base, you have utmost freedom. You can build them using the modular system at place in the game. The same logic also applies across the automated supply routes that will connect the different stations.

You can explore the procedurally generate star system and discover new resource lodes. As you expand, you’ll also have to overcome the logistic challenges coming your way. You can take on these challenges solo, or you can enjoy co-op with a buddy where each player controls a ship of their own.

Main Sequence also has a free demo on offer on Steam that you can download and try out to have a better idea of the gameplay and features.

Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023, has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities."

While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia, Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios, which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation."

In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world.

But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release. Of the remaining games, one was Marathon, which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord, one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests.

A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects:

The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven, reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress."

The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities."

#3699. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Water Temple Walkthrough

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Well, you’ve made it. You’re finally at the most infamous dungeon in all of Zelda-dom, the Water Temple of Ocarina of Time. Good news for you: In the remake, this dungeon is far, far easier than it’s ever been. A few of the edges have been sanded down, the rooms all look far more distinct and memorable so it’s less of a mental maze, and the iron boots can be equipped and de-equipped simply by pressing down on the gamepad. Compared to the original, it’s a smooth ride. But still, this is one of the most involved dungeons in the game, so buckle on that Zora Tunic and let’s get swimming.

To enter the Water Temple, you need to be wearing (no, I wasn’t joking) the Zora Tunic, which you get by freeing King Zora from his ice block back in Zora Domain. To do that, you need Blue Fire in a bottle, which you obtain in the Ice Cavern as an adult. You’ll also need the Iron Boots from that same cavern. If you haven’t gotten that far yet, back yourself up and come back to this guide later.

Once you’re in the temple, remove your iron boots and float to the top. Run forward, and you’ll be in a big, open room with a bunch of doors on all four sides across four different floors, and water below you. I’m going to be referring to this as the “main hall” going forward. We’re going to be here a lot. I’ll also be referring to doors by floor and cardinal direction, so if you’re ever confused about what I’m talking about, open that map.

The first thing you’re going to do is slay that Blue Tektite in front of you. Sword, hookshot, whatever you like, just get it out of the way.

Next, you’re going to equip those Iron Boots, descend to the first floor, and head through the east door. Once you’re inside, remove the boots to float upward for a cutscene with your fiancee, Ruto. When it’s over, grab the Dungeon Map from the chest in front of you, and then stand on the platform with the Triforce symbol and play Zelda’s Lullaby to lower the water level.

Real quick tip: There are three different spots to mess with the water level in this dungeon, and each one will raise it to a different spot. This one brings it down to the first floor, and is marked by glowy blue pillars. It might be good to make a note somewhere of which color results in which water level, just in case you ever get turned around or confused and the water level is in the wrong place.

Once the water has dropped, fearlessly jump down the hole, landing in the water below so it doesn’t damage you. Now, with the water taken care of, note that one of the torches in here is lit. Stand behind it with your bow equipped and aim an arrow through the fire to each of the two torches on the other end of the room to open the door in front of you, then enter. Defeat the three Spikes by blocking their attacks with your shield and swinging your sword when they’re vulnerable to obtain a Small Key. (Din’s Fire is also usable for this puzzle).

Backtrack the way you came in and head out into the main hall. There are two more aptly named Spikes out here waiting for you; get rid of them. To your left (west side, 1F) is a bombable/breakable wall. Knock that out, and use your Iron Boots to sink, sink, sink. Head down the underwater corridor and take care of the Shell Blade by hitting it with your hookshot when its mouth is all the way open. At the end of the corridor, take off the boots and rise up.

In here, climb the platform jutting out of the water and use the hookshot to grapple onto the pillars ahead of you. Take down the Tektites and the Like Like (Hookshot is great here), and you’ll be rewarded with the Compass. Now, all the way back to the main hall!

To the west (1F) is a block you can push forward until it drops in the water. Do that, then use the boots to sink again. Look out for the Shell Blade in the way, then rise back up at the end of the hall. You’ll find yourself in a room with a whirlpool and some statues underwater, and a chest on the other side.

This looks trickier than it is. Use the iron boots to drop into the whirlpool, aiming for the center platform (the serpent’s body) stretched down the middle of the pool. Stand on the platform and use your hookshot to smack the weird gem thing in the serpent’s mouth. This will unlock the underwater grate, allowing you to enter. You might need to don and doff the iron boots a few times to swim over properly, but with some careful aiming it’s very doable. There are two more Shell Blades to fight inside, after which you’re free to take off the boots, rise to the surface, and grab the small key.

Back across the whirlpool, out the door, into the main hall again. There’s a locked door on the central pillar here, directly in front of you, and you now have a key. Head inside.

Once inside, step forward, turn around, and look up for a grapple point. Use your hookshot to get on the platform above. Right in front of you is a spot to stand and play Zelda’s Lullaby to raise the water back up. (Note: the columns here are green, green brings the water to 2F! Write it down if you need to!) Before you leave this inside pillar, though, jump in the water and look down: a new gap has opened up with the water level rising.

Use iron boots to drop down, where three Spikes are waiting for you. Kill them with the hookshot, then use the hookshot to hit the green switch above your head, releasing a Shell Blade. Kill that too, then remove the iron boots where it was standing to rise up into the now-open area. There’s a red rupee in a chest on the way up, as well as a gold skulltula on the wall opposite. Funny, I feel like something else used to be here in the original game…anyway, grab these, backtrack the way you came in, and take off the boots to rise back up into the middle of the pillar. Then swim out the door into the main hall.

Directly in front of you across the water (2F, east side) is a bombable/hammerable wall in an alcove. You know what to do. Smash the pots for bombs if needed, otherwise use the Megaton Hammer if you’ve cleared the Fire Temple already, and head on through.

Be cautious as you head into the water and equip the Iron Boots. There are four Stingers waiting for you. Your hookshot will take care of them, but it’s easy to get overwhelmed, so take it slow (not that you can do otherwise with those boots on). Once they’re dead, proceed to the end of the underwater hallway and unequip the boots to rise to the surface.

In front of you is a pool of water with a switch in it, and a round platform being lifted by a fountain. Use your hookshot to hit the switch to lower the platform, stand on the platform, then use hookshot again on the same switch to raise yourself up to the floor above. Your reward is a Small Key. Take it, then backtrack all the way to the main hall again.

In the main hall, hop in the water and swim around the central pillar to the locked door directly across from where you just entered. It’s got glowing red columns around itâcan’t miss it. Use the Small Key and head inside. Smack the switch and ready yourself; a blue Tektite will descend and try to fight you. Once it’s dispatched, stand on the lowered platform and use your hookshot to hit the switch again and rise up.

It’s another Zelda’s Lullaby spot, this time with red lights, that will bring the water to 3F! Play that same song! Up goes the water. Jump down from the ledge next to the Triforce symbol and back into the water of the main room.

Mind any Tektites you haven’t dispatched already and swim on over to 3F, west side, for another locked door for which you conveniently have a key.

A couple of Keese will be waiting for you to slash them up. Take stock of your surroundings before you proceed. You’ll want to use the hookshot to grapple your way up these moving platforms to the top, one by one. Start by dropping down to the platform below the one you start on, and it’ll descend until you can grapple across. Then just work your way up, one by one. Don’t panic, it’s very doable, and there’s a stable platform to the side you can jump to if you need a second to collect yourself. Head through the door at the top once you reach it.

In this next room, I started by hitting all the Tektites below with my arrows just to get them out of the way. Then, use your hookshot to hit the switch at the center of the room and make the grapple points raise up. You’ll want to grapple to the first point directly in front of you, then (counterintuitively) hit the switch again to lower the points. Use the grapple point on the next wall to crossâyou’ll be able to continue along the ledge only if the grapple point pillars are lowered. Hit the switch yet again and grapple to the final pillar, hit the switchÂ again to lower the pillars. Climb atop the one next to you, then hit the switch one final time to raise the pillar and lift you within reach of the next floor.

Hit those pots for health, arrows, whatever before you go through the door, it’s time for one of the best bosses in the game!

Shadow Link is tough; he mirrors your moves! Don’t attack him head-on while his shield is up or he’ll do something I hear the kids call “aura farming.” I was able to beat him pretty easily by keeping my guard up and dodging his combos, waiting for an opening. In the first phase of the fight, I would dodge to the left side twice whenever he swung, then would come in for a combo toward his exposed back. In the second phase, this was trickier, but still very doable if I dodged backwards twice and then threw out the hookshot to stun him. Make sure you dodge backwards far enough when he gears up for a spin attack, and don’t let yourself get pushed too close to the arena walls, or he can pin you down for some big damage.

With Shadow Link down, head through the door opposite where you came in (use your map if you got turned around) to finally obtain the Longshot, which will let you hookshot targets even farther away than before! To escape this room, aim for the very far away targets above you, then drop down the waterfall into the cavern below. Let yourself float down the river, but mind the whirlpoolsâyou can use the iron boots to just walk between them underwater. About three-quarters of the way down the river, there’s a gold skulltula on a wall above you. Make sure you’re firmly iron-booted underwater, then use the longshot to smack it once to defeat it, and then again to collect the token.

Climb atop the stone outcropping on the end of the river and use the longshot again, once to hit the eye above the gates and open them, and again to grapple to the grapple point on the other side of the gates before they close on you.

We’re back in familiar territory, so head out to the main hall once again. We’ve still got some work to do, and we’re sorely in want of a boss key right about now. First, we need to get the water level down. Get those boots on and drop down to 1F east, the room where you first ran into Ruto. Swim up to the Triforce and play Zelda’s Lullaby to drop the water, then head back into the main hall. Then, you want to enter the central pillar again from the door on 1F. We’re here to raise the water level, but hold up. Grapple to the Triforce stand, then look at the ceiling for a grapple point you can now reach with the longshot. Fly on up there, then look across to the other side of the ceiling for another gold skulltula. Once you have that, drop back down and play Zelda’s Lullaby.

Everything’s in place! Exit the pillar and run around the central platform to stand on the floating block, looking across at the outer wall. You should see a gate with a grapple point on the other side, and an eye switch above. Once again, use the longshot to hit the eye, then immediately use it again on the grapple to get through. Drop into the pool and equip the iron boots, then walk into the hallway. There’s a movable block wedged into the wall hereâpull it out as far as you can, blocking off the hallway, then take off the boots and swim up and out of the pool. You should be able to see a fence ahead of you with a waterfall on the other side, and a grapple point on the ceiling. Grapple to it with the longshot, use the iron boots to sink into the water, then head down the hallway and push the block out of your way to clear a path to the chest with yet another small key.

Back to the main hall again, equipping the iron boots again and sinking down to 1F, north. Grapple across the gap and use your small key on the door. Inside, there are a lot of tektites in the way. Use your sword, shield, bow, whatever, to get them out of the way (seriously, they will knock you into whirlpools otherwise). Carefully cross the room, avoiding the boulders, using the iron boots as needed to stay out of whirlpools, and go through the door. In here, use the longshot to dispatch all the stingers, then smash the rock walls (with bombs or the megaton hammer) to reveal a block that can be pushed into the water to hit a switch. The switch will raise the water level for you to head out the door in the wall above.

Whew. Almost done. In here, step on the switch to raise platforms you can jump across, and a tektite with them. Get rid of it (and the other tektite on the other side of the room) as you see fit, then cross and go through the opening. On the other side, be careful. Boulders are rolling down this stream and will run you over if you step in at the wrong time. Wait for one to pass, then go under the waterfall and immediately turn to the left to jump into the alcove. There’s a shell blade waiting, so get that out of the way. Before you head through the door, turn back, wait for the boulder to pass, then jump back in the stream, through the waterfall, and look upâthere’s another gold skulltula near the ceiling. Grab it fast, then turn back and head through the door to, at long last, claim the boss key.

Great work, folks! Turn back, follow the boulders down the stream and into the room you were in earlier with the boulders and whirlpools, then back into the main hall. I’m sorry to say we’ve got to mess with the water levels one more time. You’ll need to go back into 2F west, head up the fountain, and play Zelda’s Lullaby one last time to raise the water and open a path up the big stairs to the north on 2F (technically 3F). Drop down, and head that direction. You’ll have to stand on the platform of the central pillar and longshot your way over. Load up on hearts from the pots before you go in, and get ready to fight.

Okay, not yet. Use your iron boots in this room to climb the waterfall and avoid the spiky things spinning back and forth.Â Now get ready to fight!

Morpha isn’t too bad, as bosses go. The boss itself is the weird red Metroid-looking ball thingie that’s hiding in the tentacles. Your main goal is to use the longshot to rip it out of its watery protection and whack it a bunch with your sword. This is pretty easy with Navi’s targeting; the main thing you need to worry about is getting hit by water tentacles. Morpha will manifest these out of the water and try and slam them on the ground near you. Early on, they’ll be pretty spread out, but later in the fight they’ll form a big wall that’s harder to avoid. If you get trapped you can also use the grapple points on the sides of the room to fly out of danger. I tried to stay on the edges as much as possible; you never really want to be in the water with Morpha. But you can use the central platforms to bait Morpha into an easier spot for you to longshot the ball out, or just to cross out of the way of attacks. Try to be aware of where Morpha the Ball is at all times, as this fight can get annoying if it’s always all the way across the room, just out of range. Use those grapple points!

That’s the Water Temple done, folks! Enjoy the cutscenes, and get the heck outta there to see how the Zora are doing.

Oh, psst. Once the cutscenes are over, you’ll be at Lake Hylia, just before sunrise. Check out the stone monument in front of you to make good use of that timing. You’re welcome!

#3698. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

UPDATE: And the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store history.

UPDATE 11TH NOVEMBER: Grand Theft Auto 6 has also become the most pre-ordered game "of all time" on the Xbox Store, Microsoft has announced. And on that platform, again, the advice is to pre-load because of "unprecedented demand" for the game, a post on Xbox Wire said.

The Xbox difference is that you can use Xbox Cloud to stream GTA 6 to other Xbox devices, although not PC, notably - the game isn't available on PC and presumably Rockstar doesn't want it playable there by any means. Microsoft's stream-deal with Rockstar has also expanded to include Red Dead Redemption 2 "and more", which will be available to stream in the "coming months".

ORIGINAL STORY 10TH NOVEMBER: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

Have you managed to resist pre-ordering it yet?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Before the Arrowverse existed, fans had a Superman show without Superman called Smallville, and that series defined my childhood. Now, it’s celebrating it’s 25th anniversary (and making me feel old). The series focuses squarely on Clark Kent, and it makes some interesting choices regarding the DC mythos. Interestingly, the show never saw Tom Welling's Clark fully suited up as the Man of Steel, and the actor himself shared some BTS details about why that was the case.

Just to refresh fans' memories, Clark never wore the classic red-and-blue suit, and barely hit the skies. However, the final moment gave a little wink at who this fan-favorite Clark Kent had become by showing him running across the rooftop of the Daily Planet and ripping open his shirt to reveal the classic S on the chest. This was the closest fans came to seeing the actor in the hero tights.

When Welling and his co-star, Michael Rosenbaum, (who played Lex Luther) spoke with Variety, he revealed the reason behind the lack of a super suit:

We got to set that day, and they had given me just a T-shirt with no sleeves to wear underneath the shirt. Because they didn’t have the money to put the suit on, and they weren’t going to see it anyway.

The absence of a full suit wasn’t a major surprise, given creators Alfred Gough and Miles Millar initiated a “no flights, no tights” rule when they started the show. Only one of those was ever broken. While Welling admits that they “toed the line a few times” when it came to the suit, they never did get the actor in a pair of tights. The reason for that was pretty simple. They weren’t able to do so unless Welling gave the “all right,” and to this day, this iteration of Clark has not suited up.

Funny enough, the closest we came to seeing Clark in a hero costume was when he wore the Green Arrow suit for an episode. Years later, along with Erica Durance (who played Lois Lane), Welling did reprise his role as Clark for a scene in the Arrowverse's "Crisis on Infinite Earths” crossover event, though even by that point, the character had given up his powers and retired as a hero. Despite Kent not taking to the skies in the final shot, Welling enjoyed the series, and he had this to say about his character's status:

We can’t go with him. But he’s out there.

This is technically true, and there have also been plenty of Supermen before and after Smallville. Yet fans have remained dedicated to the series. That's partially thanks to Welling, Rosenbaum, and several cast members reuniting conventions around the country. Plus, Rosenbaum and Welling host the re-watch podcast “Talkville,” which is currently recapping Season 9. With that, fans continue to hear BTS stories and re-live their favorite moments.

While there have been other Supes shows, the former WB/CW series still stands as the only series to solely focus on Clark and not his alter ego. But this could change if Welling and Rosenbaum succeed in reviving the series. The duo have been reportedly attempting to bring back Smallville via an animated sequel, and this could potentially mean (finally) seeing Clark in the suit.

I'd still actually like to see Tom Welling don the costume in a live-action production, though, even if the chances of that happening seem slim to none. At the very least, fans can enjoy Clark's entire journey by streaming all 10 seasons of Smallville with a Hulu subscription.

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

#3694. Student Game Development Competition Shut Down Because Kids Kept Submitting AI Slop

This will be the last year for the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a competition for young people, as the entries have grown overrun with AI-generated slop. According to a report in PC Gamer the event, which has been around for 12 years, will cease operations because it was getting too difficult to determine which games were made with AI and which were made entirely by the kids themselves.

The contest was open to students from elementary to high school, and required kids either working alone or in groups of up to four people to submit a game based on a chosen theme complete with a design document and a short trailer showing off the game. On Reddit, a parent of a child who regularly submitted games to the competition lamented the competition’s shutdown. “My teenage son and his friends entered the competition for several years, meeting up regularly, discussing ideas, and working together on a shared passion project,” the parent wrote. “It gave them something exciting to work on, and a common goal to strive towards outside of school. It also gave them confidence, and made them feel part of a wider community.”

In a statement to PC Gamer, Cathy Zemaitis, head of the Student Learning and Progress division at ACER, the company that puts on the challenge, said, “The decision was driven by the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development, making it harder to judge what students made themselves, and moving the program away from its original purpose.”

The “justification” for using AI in a professional game development setting is to essentially make games faster and more cheaply. One of the stated purposes of the challenge is to “enable students to develop real-world skills.” How is that accomplished using AI tools, especially at an age when core game development skills haven’t yet been learned? I’d imagine not very effectively. And it really sucks that the example adults are setting with the push for and normalization of generative AI is resulting in the end of a valuable opportunity for the next generation to develop a skill. We are eating the game development seed corn.

“I know as adults the world can be unfair, and we need to adapt,” the parent on Reddit wrote. “But this really hit home for me, because the victims this time are children. My son was visibly gutted when I told him the news, and it genuinely felt like part of his identity had been destroyed.”

I spend way too much time on wikis reading about spin-off games made for handheld and mobile devices I will probably never play (there was a whole trilogy of Silent Hill: Orphan games that have lived up to their name by being orphaned on old phones). The Elder Scrolls Travels are a prime example—games made in the gap between Morrowind and Oblivion. The third in the series, Shadowkey, came out on Nokia's N-Gage handheld—a cross between a GameBoy Advance and a mobile phone that lasted two years before being discontinued in 2005.

This first-person RPG is about to return thanks to Dan Whelan, whose Shadowkey Reforged project will let us play Shadowkey in widescreen with controller support and upscaled graphics. You can choose to play in classic or modern mode, but you can also toggle individual features one by one. Modern mode isn't just a graphical upgrade as it also adds features from the later mainline Elder Scrolls games like stamina-based sprinting, stealth, and ragdoll physics.

This is one of those times where I prefer the original game's look, as the brutally abrupt draw distance leaves a lot to your imagination while the modernized version seems to show enemies looming unresponsively in the near distance. And it's not like the upscaled character models actually look good, despite being beyond what Nokia's taco phone was capable of displaying.

While Shadowkey was never particularly well-ranked in the pantheon of Elder Scrolls games, people did praise its use of the Morrowind soundtrack, which Shadowkey Reforged will continue. Point it to your Morrowind install and it'll borrow both music and sound effects from the best Elder Scrolls game.

To answer the obvious question, Whelan says in the FAQ: "I used AI to assist with coding and building the engine, and with debugging. I used AI image generation combined with Photoshop and some manual sprite editing to create most of the modern, higher resolution artwork."

Whelan plans to release Shadowkey Reforged on November 11, which is just 18 hours away at the time of writing. You'll be able to download Windows, Mac, and Android versions from the website, though you'll need the original game's files from your Nokia N-Gage as well, or whatever abandonware site you frequent.
