It appears the Barefoot Contessa knew a thing or two about Batman's travel plans.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I spend a lot of time keeping up with the 2026 movie schedule and all the upcoming superhero movies, but Jennifer Garner left me thinking about a Batman production from a decade ago. The actress recently shared a fond memory involving Ben Affleck, Ina Garten and an unforgettable family trip to Paris. I love that the Caped Crusader barely scratches the surface of what made it so special.

During a conversation on Happy Hour with Ina Garten, the 13 Going on 30 actress recalled taking her children overseas while Affleck was filming in London. Apparently, the comic book movie production provided the perfect excuse to get out of town for a while. Garner explained:

When my kids were little, I went to Paris. Ben was shooting some Batman-ish movie in London, and we went for six weeks. I took them out of school. It was the last time I really took kids out of school, but it was wonderful. It was incredible. It was so fun.

I recently revisited Affleck and Garner's time making Daredevil together, so hearing her describe his later superhero blockbuster as some "Batman-ish movie" is especially funny. I imagine Affleck had a few more specific words for the project, but I appreciate Garner remembers the family adventure rather than whatever Bruce Wayne was getting up to at the time.

Her timing also helps identify the film. While Justice League arrived in theaters in 2017, Affleck and the production spent months filming in London the previous year. Reports from that April confirmed that Garner and their three children planned to stay in the U.K. during production. By May, the family had also been spotted vacationing in Paris. So, despite the wonderfully vague description, Justice League appears to be our Batman-ish culprit.

There's a bittersweet wrinkle to the timeline. Garner and Affleck announced their separation in 2015, before the trip, and officially filed for divorce in 2017. Their divorce was finalized the following year. That makes this a particularly sweet memory of their family life during a complicated period. The two have maintained a close co-parenting relationship since, with Garner recently praising Affleck for helping care for their children while she works.

Apparently, we have Ina Garten to thank for one of Garner's favorite memories from the trip. With her youngest son, Samuel, only 4 at the time, Garner shared photos of the kids with Garten, who suggested they take a boat ride along the Seine. Really, who am I to argue with the Barefoot Contessa about how to spend an afternoon in Paris?

Garner recalled cruising down the river as the city began lighting up around them, and the experience stuck with her. She's since made a point of doing it whenever she returns to Paris, and looking back at those original photos still reminds her of how happy the kids were. She told Garten that her suggestion made the whole thing "such an adventure." I love that something as simple as taking a boat ride became one of those family memories she keeps coming back to.

Garten's Paris recommendations didn't stop there. Years later, when Garner returned with her eldest daughter Violet, she texted her friend for another round of suggestions. This time Garten sent them to a handbag boutique, a cheese shop, a specialty food market and a restaurant specializing in soufflés. Violet apparently enjoyed the itinerary so much that she retraced their steps while studying abroad. Now I'm wondering how I get Ina Garten's number before my next vacation.

I like hearing Garner speak so fondly about those days, especially knowing what was happening in her personal life at the time. It also makes me wonder how many wonderful family memories get made while Hollywood's biggest productions happen in the background.

Affleck might have been busy bringing his take on The Dark Knight to life; his wife and kids were apparently having an adventure all their own. Something tells me those Paris photographs mean a whole lot more to her than another superhero movie ever could.

#3632. Switch 2 Just Had Its Best Sales Week Of 2026, And It’s All Because Of Zelda

Nintendo just released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake for Switch 2, and the themed console that Nintendo debuted with the game has, perhaps unsurprisingly, sold incredibly well.

Circana's Mat Piscatella shared new data that confirms the Switch 2 just had its best sales week of 2026 so far, based on dollar sales, thanks to the 40th Anniversary Edition console. The $520 console launched on October 29, and Circana's reporting period for the week ended on October 31.

The special-edition console sports a geometric design inspired by the Zelda series, with a large Triforce symbol on the dock. The accompanying Joy-Cons feature the game's classic green and gold color scheme, along with specific designs based on the RPG series.

The system doesn't include a copy of the game, which launched on November 5, and is priced at $60 digitally and $70 on a physical cartridge.

Sales of the 40th Anniversary Edition console helped lift total spending on hardware in the US for the week by 81% compared to the same week in 2025.

The Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge hit critically, scoring a 9/10 here at GameSpot. It's the highest-rated game of 2026 so far. Nintendo has not revealed any sales numbers for the game, however.

#3631. Kate Middleton, Prince William, King Charles, and Queen Camilla Gather For Remembrance Day

This Sunday, November 8, King Charles III, Queen Camilla, Kate Middleton, Prince William, Princess Anne and other members of the royal family came together to observe Remembrance Sunday, one of the most solemn events on the United Kingdom's calendar. The day marks the anniversary of the armistice that ended World War I, signed on “the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month” in 1918.

The focal point of every Remembrance Day is the Cenotaph in Whitehall, the Portland stone monument where tribute is paid to those who fell in the wars and conflicts in which the country has participated. Every year, representatives of the royal family, political leaders, the Armed Forces, and veterans gather there: This year, more than 10,000 marched alongside the king and the prime minister.

True to tradition, Charles III laid a wreath at the memorial on behalf of the nation and led the royal family. At his side was Prince William, Princess Anne, and the Duke of Edinburgh, who also paid their respects with a floral tribute. Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales, Kate Middleton, watched the ceremony from the balcony of the Foreign Office, as is customary. On the political front, Prime Minister Andy Burnham laid a wreath on his first Remembrance Sunday as head of the government, accompanied by Opposition Leader Kemi Badenoch and other political leaders.

The day before had already been a day of remembrance: the King, the Queen, and the Princes of Wales attended the Festival of Remembrance at the Royal Albert Hall, the major tribute to the armed forces that precedes Remembrance Sunday.

#3630. 'DWTS' Grammy Night Reveals Which Couples Are Going to Semifinals

Dancing With the Stars is one week closer to crowning a season 35 champion, with the semifinalists officially revealed after Grammy Night.

The Tuesday, November 10, episode kicked off with a sultry Argentine tango from Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach, followed by a fiery paso doble from Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov. The judges were impressed with both routines, but Carrie Ann Inaba said she caught Glenn’s foot come off the floor at one point.

Before her own Argentine tango, Maura Higgins experienced a scary rib injury during rehearsals, which made her even more worried about being “on the chopping block.” The Traitors alum broke down in vulnerable moment in the rehearsal studio, but her determination paid off — she and Mark Ballas earned 27 out of 30 points.

Jenna Dewan then hit the ballroom for her Janet Jackson-inspired jazz number, earning a celebratory message from the pop icon herself. “Weren’t those such fun times we had back then during those days [on] the All for You tour? I miss you. … You’re gonna do an incredible job, I know it,” Jackson told Dewan, who previously performed as one of her backup dancers. “Let’s get together when I’m back in L.A.”

When it was time for the dance-offs, the ballroom welcomed live performances of “The Boy Is Mine” by Brandy and Monica, “The Middle” by Maren Morris and “All I Wanna Do” by Sheryl Crow.

Eventually, however, one couple was forced to say farewell. Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy were eliminated ahead of the semifinals.

“Honestly, dancing again, getting to share my joy with my family … I had a great time. And I loved getting to share that with the world. All love,” the actress said at the end of the episode.

Eufy’s Essential 7-Piece Alarm System is down to $269.98 at Amazon from $399.99, a $130 discount that price trackers say is its lowest price ever. The kit includes a HomeBase Mini hub with 64GB of built-in storage, a keypad, four entry sensors, and a motion sensor. That’s enough to cover the front and back doors, a couple of ground-floor windows, and a main hallway in an apartment or smaller house. It also doesn’t require a subscription, so once you’ve paid for the system, you won’t have to worry about ongoing monthly fees.

With the sensors in place, you’ll get an instant notification through the free Eufy app whenever someone opens a protected door or window, while the motion sensor can detect movement in areas like a living room or hallway. Not everyone in the household needs the app to use the system, though, since the included keypad lets family members or a house sitter arm and disarm it right at the door. Everything connects back to the HomeBase Mini, which serves as the central hub with built-in storage that keeps everything stored locally.

Setting up the system takes minutes, as the battery-powered sensors require no wiring and the app guides you through each step once the HomeBase is plugged in. That said, you will need to replace the sensor batteries periodically, and a larger home with several entrances may require more than the four entry sensors and one motion sensor included in the kit—you can add more Eufy sensors and accessories as needed, but each comes at an extra cost. And if you want to see what triggered an alert, you'll have to purchase compatible cameras separately, since no cameras are included in the package.

#3628. GTA 6 Preorder Numbers Are So Good, Even Take-Two Is Struggling To Believe Them

Grand Theft Auto 6 looks set to be the best-selling game of 2026, and even publisher Take-Two Interactive is surprised at just how big the demand for it has been ahead of launch. In its second-quarter fiscal year 2027 results, Take-Two was bullish on the sales numbers for the game, but it has only slightly adjusted its forecast for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.

"Preorders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking far above our initial expectations, and we know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough," Take-Two said. Originally, the publisher had predicted to make $7.9 – $8.1 billion in its current financial year, and it has increased this figure to $7.98 – $8.18 billion. Speaking to GamesIndustry.Biz, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the reason for the modest increase was due to GTA 6's launch being so close.

"[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we’re making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the preorders are far exceeding our original expectations," Zelnick said. "We’re maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we’ll know a lot more after the release. We’re just not updating our numbers right now because we are so close to the launch. However, preorders are far exceeding our expectations."

Back in August, a third-party research company estimated that GTA 6 had already brought in more than $400 million in revenue from 4.38 million preorders, and with its launch just days away, that figure has certainly grown even more. Take-Two had previously spoken about the unprecedented preorder numbers it was experiencing for the game--while not sharing any concrete numbers--and so far, it looks like the $100 edition is a very popular option. Experts also believe that the majority of preorders will come in the week before launch.

So, like many other MCU stars awaiting Secret Wars filming, the man has been trying to stay fit. He recently took a note from Inde Navarette when it comes to Marvel workouts, and trolled Saturday Night Live’s recent Shane Gillis gaffe in the same video.

I’m sure Marvel was super happy about getting roped in to the Shane Gillis monologue controversy, which involved the Tires star joking about women wearing little clothing at the gym these days. (He also capped these comments by calling them “whores,” which is probably what made the story go as viral as it did.) Anyway, Shane Gillis made the joke at Studio 8H, and then a week later Inde Navarette referenced it while talking about working out to play one of the X-Men in her own SNL monologue.

This is where Simu Liu comes in. The man came out of the wood work this week to cheekily show off a gym workout. He superimposed the video with Inde Navarette’s SNL monologue comments, and captioned the video, “time to put on my little outfit…”

Listen, this isn’t the first time Simu Liu has had a little fun trolling on the Internet, and I feel confident in guessing it won’t be the last. Just a couple of months ago he had a little fun with the MCU movies in order, and asked fans to “please help [him] support this little indie feature,” above a poster for Avengers: Doomsday, which will likely make over a billion dollars. Then, there was that time he joked about the Spider-Man leaks when Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire were involved in one of Tom Holland's popular films.

He can take it as well as dish it out, though. Early in his career, he modeled for some stock photos, and the Internet LOVES to bring it up. But he's taken the comments on the chin.

Right now, Marvel is in between films, so if you’re going to troll about the MCU, now’s a good time for a star to get a little attention for it. While schlepping relatively low weights is not as impressive as, say, one-armed pull-ups, it’s a good way to keep the fanbase engaged as Doomsday gets closer.

Avengers: Doomsday hits the 2026 release schedule around the holidays, and is in theaters opposite Dune 3, which has earned it the moniker Dunesday. Meanwhile, Chris Hemsworth has remained swole, and it has people wondering if he’s getting ready for Secret Wars. On the other hand, Simu Liu has already confirmed he's in both.

#3626. LACMA Art+Film Gala: Nicole Kidman, Timothée Chalamet Honor Denis Villeneuve

“It’s a pleasure to be here. You guys are just crazy party people,” said artist Vija Celmins as she summed up the jovial atmosphere at the 15th annual LACMA Art+Film Gala during her casual and off-the-cuff acceptance speech as one of the two honorees that night.

The annual fundraiser is a party, and unique among the many galas that hit the town this time of year. Along with raising money for the museum’s initiative to make film more central to its programming (this year it raised a record-breaking almost $7 million), it brings out an eclectic mix of A-list talent, up-and-coming filmmakers, and giants of the art world.

Honoree, Denis Villeneuve, Honoree Vija Celmins, co-chair Eva Chow and LACMA CEO Michael Govan

Just a quick scan of the packed room: Al Pacino sitting with artist Ed Ruscha and art dealer Larry Gagosian; artist Alex Israel wrapping his arm around Orlando Bloom for a photo; model Alex Consani crouching down to chat with influencer and comedian Quenlin Blackwell; and artists Jonas Wood and Mickalene Thomas chatting in one corner while Sarah Paulson and Parker Posey catch up in another.

Anya Taylor-Joy set the mood for the evening as one of the first arrivals on the red carpet, where talent posed in front of Chris Burden’s famed public art installation Urban Light. There in support of Dune director Denis Villeneuve, who was honored along with Celmins, the Dune: Part Two star wore a vintage 1997 Pierre Cardin haute couture bridal gown with a sheer silver overlay that looked both of the past and of the future.

Villeneuve’s leading man, Timothée Chalamet, skipped the carpet altogether, instead slipping into the crowded tent for dinner in a seat next to Villeneuve and his wife, producer Tanya Lapointe. Chalamet arrived separately from girlfriend Kylie Jenner, who did walk the carpet in a low-back Ashi Studio gown. When Jenner arrived at her table, she was seated opposite Chalamet, reaching across to grab his hand.

Seated next to Villeneuve was Nicole Kidman (in a voluminous, ballerina-inspired Chanel dress), who flew 15 hours from Australia to give Villeneuve his award. “The truth is I’ve never really met Denis. I’ve met him on some red carpets and sort of waved at him,” she said during her remarks. “Yet somehow I feel like I know the deepest parts of him because that is what extraordinary filmmakers do. They let you in. They reveal themselves to us through their work. They invite you into their imaginations, into their dreams, into their questions, and into their fears.”

Monica Barbaro, Salma Hayek and Kim Kardashian

Before Villeneuve took the stage, a video capturing his film legacy of big, bold, and personal epics like Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, Arrival, and the Dune trilogy was played, featuring a slew of A-list directors singing his praises, including Steven Spielberg, Alfonso Cuarón, Alejandro González Iñárritu, James Cameron, and Chloé Zhao. “I’ve always felt that cinema is seen as a Pop art—the film carries the burden of being popular in the present,” said Villeneuve in his acceptance speech. “But at the end of the day, the real challenge is to make something that can enter the test of time.”

Speaking of tests (screen tests, that is) Villeneuve got a bit playful with the end of his speech, announcing to the room that he would—right here, right now—announce which actor would play James Bond. The French Canadian director is helming the next Bond film, and over the past week reports have been flying about who might be cast. Would Villeneuve put us all out of our misery and spill the beans? “The actor who will play the next James Bond is—and I will stop right now because [producer] Amy Pascal is about to have a heart attack,” he said with a smile.

The gala, once again presented by Gucci, hosted a slew of this Oscar season’s most exciting young filmmakers, including Obsession filmmaker Curry Barker and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman, along with La Bola Negra directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (known as Los Javis). The latter told me they didn’t plan to party as hard as they did at the Academy Museum Gala a few weeks ago, where they went viral for singing along to Taylor Swift’s performance of “Love Story.” Said Ambrossi, “I’m drinking only water tonight.”

Among the other guests at the gala (which had additional support by Audi), Joel Edgerton chatted with Abbott Elementary’s Quinta Brunson and Daniel Scheinert, one half of the Oscar-winning directing team Daniels (Everything Everywhere All at Once). Kim Kardashian wove her way through the crowd, pausing perfectly to look over her shoulder for a trailing photographer. And several stars made a date night out of the event: Sienna Miller brought fiancé Oli Green; Julia Garner sat with musician Charlie Walker; Viola Davis enjoyed the night with husband and producing partner Julius Tennon. Paris Hilton, who introduced Rosé onstage with her classic catchphrase “that’s hot,” wore a glittering Jenny Packham gown as she cascaded through the room with her husband, Carter Reum.

Eva Chow, who had co-chaired the gala for the past 15 years with Leonardo DiCaprio, announced that she’d be stepping down from her post after this year. Dubbed the “Culture Queen of Los Angeles,” she is credited with bringing together Hollywood and the art world for the event, helping grow it into the must-attend party of the season. DiCaprio couldn’t make it this year because he has a cold, but his girlfriend, model Vittoria Ceretti, was there to represent him.

But with all these big Hollywood types in the room, it was Celmins who stole the show—though she didn’t mean to. In a video that ran before her acceptance speech, the artist welcomed the video crew into her home, revealing her quick-witted humor, her ornery cat (she claims to be a dog person), and her love of Bob Dylan. Celmins is best known for her boundless work inspired by nature, including ocean waves, desert floors, and starry night skies. She charmed the crowd with her boundless personality as well.

LACMA had plenty to celebrate this year too. After a 20-year-long planning and development process, the David Geffen Galleries were completed this past year. As partygoers entered the tent for dinner, the silhouette of the formidable new building stood out in the background. “Same tent. Different buildings around it,” joked LACMA CEO Michael Govan during his opening remarks.

After his speech, Villeneuve and all the guests made their way out to LACMA’s main courtyard, where Rosé would perform under the stars. I joked with him that I thought he would make some news with that tease of a Bond casting, and then wondered if he likes being the center of attention at a gala like this. He said he values the connections he makes with other filmmakers and artists at these events. “I like talking one-on-one,” he said.

Noor Alfallah, Al Pacino, Erica Pelosini, Larry Gagosian and Ed Ruscha

While Rosé performed four songs for the black-tie-clad audience, Emily in Paris star Ashley Park and In the Heights actor Anthony Ramos swayed to her ballad “Number One Girl.” Popcorn and cotton candy were passed out to the audience, which, naturally, sang along when Rosé ended her set with her biggest hit, “APT.” Andrew Garfield led his Artificial costar Monica Barbaro by the hand through the crowd. Though the pair didn’t pose for photos on the carpet together, the couple (who have been romantically linked since 2025) spent the evening in close contact as they chatted with friends like Salma Hayek Pinault.

Villeneuve’s speech best captured the evening’s one-of-a-kind mash-up of art and film when he spoke passionately about the importance of human effort in the era of AI. “I can create something with a prompt, or I can go into the desert with actors, with a crew, and go on a real adventure where I learn about life and become better at my craft,” he said. “More important than the result is the process. The process is how the human experience acquires its meaning. In this moment in time, it is more important than ever that human beings keep making art together.”

Odessa A'zion in a Charles & Ron + Maison Privee coat.

#3625. GTA 5 Simply Refuses To Stop Selling, Even With GTA 6 On The Way

As Grand Theft Auto 6 gets ready to launch, GTA 5 is still selling impressively. The GTA series has sold more than 480 million copies, with GTA 5 making up 235 million of those. Take-Two Interactive, the publisher, recently shared that another 5 million copies of GTA 5 were sold in the past 90 days during its second-quarter fiscal year 2027 update.

There are several reasons why GTA 5 keeps selling so well. One big factor is its frequent discounts on digital stores, and bundles with Shark Cards often cost less than buying in-game currency by itself. The game has also launched on three generations of consoles, and GTA Online has attracted a huge audience. Excitement for GTA 6 is probably helping sales too, putting GTA 5 just behind Tetris and Minecraft as one of the best-selling games ever.

Rockstar’s other major open-world game, Red Dead Redemption 2, has also reached an impressive milestone. It has sold 89 million copies, putting it just behind GTA 5 and ahead of other big titles like Wii Sports (82.9 million), Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (80.46 million), and PUBG: Battlegrounds (75 million). Whether GTA 6 will surpass these numbers is still unknown, but Take-Two Interactive is optimistic as preorders for the November 19 launch are already higher than expected.

Take-Two hasn’t released exact numbers yet, but says preorders have been “unprecedented” across the industry. Preloading is now available, and the game will be ready to play at midnight next week wherever you are.

#3624. This Autonomous Camera Robot Is My New Best Friend

Like any pure-hearted geek, I've wanted to own a droid ever since I saw Star Wars as a kid. Now, I actually have one: It's Beni, a new gadget from Mondo Robotics, and it has me saying, "Artoo who?" It's not just my Upgrade of the Week; it's possibly the upgrade of my life.

Beni is an all-terrain camera robot that was born as a project on Kickstarter, but unlike so many other Kickstarted projects, it's actually really cool. It takes 4K video while autonomously following its subject wherever they go. If you want to get action footage, there's no need to hassle with a tripod or another person: You can control it with a remote, or you can make it follow you. It can also be set to track you from the side or circle you, and you can adjust what it is doing from the app or remote control on the fly, so with minimal effort, there's no limit to the kind of elaborate shots it can pull off. Plus it's adorable. Just look at this little guy:

Being cute wouldn't matter if Beni was just a gimmick, but the footage it takes is actually really impressive. Check out this clip, which I recorded with no planning of any sort; I just locked Beni's camera on this skater and told it to follow him wherever:

See how smoothly it glides over the uneven concrete? How effortlessly it handles inclines? I even launched it off a huge ramp and it landed on the other side, righted itself, and got back to business.

Here's an example of the kind of footageyou'll get when you put it in "circle you" mode (and again, this was recorded with no prior planning):

The way it just slides under that bench? Come ON. That's just slick.

Yes, Beni is a slightly silly product, but as slightly silly products go, it's pretty inarguably awesome. Here is a short list of things I love about Beni:

It's super easy-to-use. I got it up and running moments after taking it out of the box and downloading the app. You can easily figure out how it works on the fly.

It's a multi-terrain robot. You can get an extra set of bigger, beefier wheels, but even with the stock tires, this thing worked great on uneven concrete, grass, and dirt.

It's rugged. While Beni does have obstacle detection ability, it runs into things a lot anyway, but that's not a problem. Beni can take massive, epic spills, slam into walls, and get kicked by children, and it will right itself and proceed on without a hitch. It's amazing to watch.

It actually works the way you expect it to. I know that's a low bar to clear, but it's rare for a flashy piece of tech to actually do what it says it promises, and Beni does.

It's adorable. A lot of work went into making Beni as friendly-looking as possible—it does tricks, blinks its "eyes," responds to gestures, and you can even give him a little baseball cap. Beni's vibe is positive.

It's great for social interaction. If you have a little robot following you around, people will want to talk to you. I'm not a huge fan of people, but if you want to make friends at the park, this robot will at least open the door.

It's not as expensive as you might imagine. Beni will run you $750 for the base model, and $899 for the "Explore Combo" with larger wheels, a charging stand, and a little hat. While $750 isn't cheap, for what you get, it's actually a pretty solid deal. Everything costs a fortune now anyway! You deserve a robot.

Beni isn't quite ready to make its debut yet. Right now, you can pre-order one on Mondo Robotics site, with a release planned for some time in early November. This is the company's first product, so it's not yet clear if Beni will ever be sold via third-party retailers like Amazon.

#3623. Patrick Mahomes Reacts to Fan Claiming 'He Was Done' After 3rd Child

Patrick Mahomes is ready to welcome his fourth child with wife Brittany Mahomes, responding to a fan who claimed he was “done” after his third.

“I thought Patrick said he was done after the last one,” the fan commented on a joint baby no. 4 Instagram announcement shared by Patrick, 31, and Brittany, 31, on Tuesday, November 10. The comment prompted the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback to reply, “ayyy chill chill,” before adding three laughing-crying emojis.

The fan’s comment had referred to Patrick speaking about his growing family to reporters in July 2024. “I’m done. I’ll say that. I did three and I’m done,” he told members of the press according to the Associated Press at the time. (Brittany gave birth to the couple’s third child, daughter Golden, 21 months, in January 2025.)

Patrick’s amused reaction to the fan’s reminder sparked further discussion between social media fans. “People are allowed to change their minds,” wrote one fan, while another added, “Words said by almost every parent.”

Patrick’s mom, Randi Mahomes, meanwhile only had praise for the happy news. “I cannot wait!! Congratulations, love y’all,” she commented on the joint post.”

Brittany and Patrick’s announcement featured a string of photos of the couple’s children, Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, gathered around their mom by the beach while placing their hands on her belly. “Another blessing from God,” the couple captioned the post. “& then there were 6.”

The official NFL and Chiefs Instagram accounts shared congratulatory words in the comments section, while fellow Chiefs star Travis Kelce’s official “New Heights” podcast account also wrote “Congratulations” and added four heart emojis.

The couple’s news came as a surprise to fans of Brittany, also, after the WAG had similarly stated publicly once that she was unsure about welcoming further children into her family. During a June 2025 episode of the “Whoops” podcast, Brittany said, “’We’re done, we’re done for a while. I don’t know. I mean, I feel like you can never say you’re done. I think three is all I need.”

The doting mom revealed an everlasting tribute to her family on her arm recently, sharing a photo of a tattoo that showed the side profiles of her three children connected to “Patrick’s initials into their names and birthdays.”

She said of the September 29 Instagram Story reveal, “I guess I never have showed my tattoo and people are so intrigued.”

Patrick and Brittany met in high school and began dating in 2012. Eight years later, they tied the knot in March 2022 in Maui, Hawaii, after Patrick had popped the question in a private suite inside Arrowhead Stadium, the Chiefs’ home ground.

It's been a wild week for fans of the superhero genre. Yesterday the internet exploded when it was revealed that James Gunn and Peter Safran were stepping down as co-CEOS of DC Studios, and there are countless questions about how upcoming DC movies and shows will be affected. Some fan reacts are making me especially concerned about Lanterns (which is streaming with a HBO Max subscription) and more.

Gunn's tenure as DC's head has been cut short, and it's unclear if the first slate of projects called Gods and Monsters will still move forward. The director/writer/producer took to social media with a statement about his departure, and some of the responses on Threads are cutting me to the core. Case in point: the following response which has a whopping 1.8k likes.

Goddammit, we're never getting another Lanterns season are we?

Well, now I'm depressed. Ever since its first season ended, fans have been wondering if Lanterns would get a second season on HBO. After all, there's plenty more Green Lantern lore to explore, with the writer Venessa Baden Kelly interested in bringing in Kilowog to the series. Unfortunately, Gunn's departure might put the show's second season in jeopardy, especially after Lanterns was the subject of fan backlash.

This isn't the only depressing fan response to James Gunn's threads post. Another one that's hitting hard and has over 900 likes reads:

We're never getting a full DC run ever. 😭

Ouch. While the Marvel Cinematic Universe has become a well-oiled machine over its nearly two decades in theaters, the same can't be said for things at DC. The former DCEU began with Zack Snyder's movies, which quickly put the Justice League together rather than methodically giving them solo movies. Unfortunately that shared universe started becoming less and less interconnected over the years, eventually ending with Aquaman 2.

James Gunn and Peter Safran were hoping to make a more cohesive franchise with the DCU, and there were a number of thrilling crossovers in the first few titles. While we'll still get to see a number of characters collide when Man of Tomorrow hits theaters next summer, it's unclear exactly how the burgeoning shared universe will continue afterward. For hardcore superhero fans, it feels like we'll never get a DC counterpart to the MCU, which is super depressing.

Right now there are more questions about the DCU than answers. Gunn and Safran were replaced by former Marvel executive and producer Jeremy Latcham, who obviously has experience in the genre. We'll just have to wait and see what comes next.

The next DC movie hitting theaters is Man of Tomorrow on July 9, 2027. For now fans can see Clayface in theaters as part of the 2026 movie release list.

#3621. Nintendo’s New Gift-Giving Feature Comes With Some Very Nintendo Restrictions

A new update is available for all Nintendo Switch 2 and Switch consoles, and if you're on a Nintendo Account family plan, version 23.5.0 will allow you to once again gift games to members in your group.

"Just in time for the holidays, a new feature will let family group members gift digital games to other members of their group," Nintendo wrote in an update. "You will be able to gift digital products that you purchase through Nintendo eShop on your device to family group members. This includes eligible games as well as DLC and upgrade packs."

In typical Nintendo fashion, what should be a straightforward program does have some strange restrictions. The company has noted that not every item is eligible for digital gifting and that the number of digital gifts handed out within a specific period is limited. This isn't the first time that Nintendo has offered a digital gifting program, as way back in the Wii era, owners of the console could visit the Wii Shop and grab some WiiWare or Virtual Console games. From there, users were free to gift them to anyone on their Wii friend list. That service was eventually closed after the Wii Shop Channel was shut down in 2019.

To gift someone in your family group a game, you'll need to visit the Nintendo eShop on your Switch console, find the product page, and select the "Give as a Gift" box before you check out. Select the lucky recipient, complete your purchase, and they'll receive a nice little surprise.

In related Nintendo news, the Switch 2 just had its best sales week of 2026, thanks to one plucky console dressed in green. The launch of the limited-edition Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 console--which costs $520 and doesn't include a copy of the Zelda game it's inspired by--proved to be easy money for Nintendo, as it contributed to an 81% total hardware spend increase in the US for the week, compared to the same week in 2025. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake also launched last week, and it's currently the highest-rated game of 2026.

#3620. This Pricey New Accessory Gives Your Kindle a Feature That Used to Be Standard

It has been 14 years since Amazon made a Kindle e-reader without a touchscreen, and while I certainly don't miss the days of slowly paging through my e-book library with the arrow keys on my Kindle Keyboard, the move to touch navigation did have one unfortunate result, at least for a small subset of readers: the loss of physical page-turn buttons. Once standard on all Kindles, they eventually became a premium feature available only on the pricey Kindle Oasis, before being dropped from the lineup entirely when that device was retired in 2024.

While this fall's overhaul of the Kindle lineup introduced upgrades like a metal enclosure and a flush-front design, Amazon hasn't exactly reintroduced physical buttons, but the company has launched a new accessory to appeal to the roughly 5% of the market that loves buttons (per Kevin Keith, Amazon's vice president in charge of Kindle), which essentially turns your new Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition into a Kindle Oasis: the Kindle Page-Turn Cover.

Releasing alongside the new flush-front Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition, the Page-Turn Cover is made of plant-based leather (in one of three colors to match your Kindle—Graphite, Fig, or Seaglass Green) with a magnetic front flap, a soft interior, and a right-hand bezel made of lightly textured plastic that houses two thin, elongated buttons. When you slot your compatible Kindle into the case, connecting it magnetically and via the built-in pogo pins, it will automatically pair with the device, allowing you to turn pages with a button press instead of a tap.

By default, the top button will advance you forward by one page, and the bottom button will do the reverse, though you can change which does which in your device settings. While the physical buttons on some Boox and Barnes & Noble Nook devices allow you to map different functions—like skipping an entire chapter or scrubbing through a book quickly—to a long-press or double-tap, as of this writing, the Page-Turn Cover will only let you turn one page at a time. The buttons also only work for turning pages; you'll still navigate your library and the device menus using the touchscreen.

If you're a lefty, or prefer to swap which hand you use to hold your e-reader, you can change up the orientation by turning off Lock Rotation on your device; when you flip it over to hold in your other hand, the text will automatically reorient itself, and the buttons will continue to work with your existing settings.

You might think that changing pages with an accessory would slow down your device, but in my testing, the Page-Turn Cover actually seems to turn pages faster than tapping the touchscreen. Though the new Kindles are quite speedy, there's still a perceptible lag between when you tap the screen and when the display changes to a new page. Not so with the Page-Turn Cover attached; although the very first page turn after attaching it is a bit laggy, after that it is basically instantaneous. I can't imagine this will be a game-changer for anyone—the difference is a mere fraction of a second—but it's worth noting all the same.

While this is Amazon's clever solution to satisfy the physical button die-hards without overhauling the design of its entire lineup, it does come at a cost to the reader—a literal cost: The Page-Turn Cover is around $80, and it's only compatible with the $250 Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition or the $320 Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition, the only models with the metal backing, pogo pins, and accelerometer necessary for the case to function.

In short, that means if you want a Kindle with physical buttons, you'll have to shell out at least $330, or $80 more than the third-generation Kindle Oasis cost when it launched back in 2019. (For what it's worth, you can get the Oasis-like Boox Go 7, one of my picks for the top non-Kindle e-readers, for around $270).

While most people probably don't think twice about tapping the screen to turn the page, some folks just prefer the feel of tactile buttons or would rather not have to worry about holding their device wrong and accidentally jumping forward a chapter or two.

If you've made do without them so far, you probably aren't missing them, but if you're an old-school e-reader (or just a particularly tactile person), they are definitely a nice bonus. Are they worth an $80 upgrade? That's going to depend on the reader.

#3618. Big Walk’s AI Usage Was Tiny, But Its Disclosure Has Sparked A Bigger Debate

Big Walk developer House House has confirmed that it used AI during the "final stretch" of its development. The studio recently updated its FAQs page to confirm its use of the tech, with the news coming after 19 Independent Games Festival jurors announced they'll decline to vote for "any game that uses generative AI in any capacity" during the 2027 awards show.

House House hasn't confirmed if its admittance was connected to the IGF--the IGF hasn't named any games either--and the studio said to Aftermath that it estimates "that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code" was built with AI. "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalization of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable.' We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologize that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards," House House said. The developer also mentioned that AI was used as a last resort for solving technical issues, as even an engineer at Unity--the engine that Big Walk was developed in--believed that one of their problems wasn't possible to solve.

There's a lot to unpack here, starting with why House House didn't disclose the use of AI for Big Walk. The game is hosted on platforms like Steam, where studios can voluntarily disclose AI usage when it comes to generated code (however, it is mandatory to disclose if a game has AI-generated assets), but House House says it only did so after the topic became a matter of public interest. It also added that it will continue to support developers looking to limit "the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world."

Pathologic 2 localization writer Bruno Diaz also touched on the controversy, explaining that IGF rules required studios to disclose the use of AI in development. Game designer Austin Walker posted online that the IGF committee has been debating the use of AI in game development, leading 19 jurors to issue a statement. While the group says it doesn't speak for the entire IGF organization or all jurors involved in the IGF Awards, IGF leadership supports the statement. Overall, if AI is used in any part of a game's development, from coding to visual assets, the jurors will not vote for it.

"Programming is a creative discipline whose labor deserves the same respect we extend to any part of making a game," the IGF juror's statement reads. "This extends to the past work used to train these models without the creators' consent."

The IGF's stance comes as the discussion over AI heats up in the games industry. Proponents argue it'll make video game development faster and more affordable; others argue it contributes to environmental harm and is leading to job losses across multiple fields. Others have argued that House House's use of AI to solve challenging coding bugs isn't a big deal, but critics say the AI disclosure should have been there from the beginning.

At the same time, the frequency of AI slop games has exploded in recent months, with the October edition of Steam Next Fest being a dumping ground for hastily vibe-coded game demos. Copycats have also become a major headache, with several game developers withdrawing their demos from the public over fears that bad actors will copy their work and rush a clone to market.

#3616. These Are the Best Arc Browser Alternatives, Now That It's Shutting Down

Khamosh Pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

Well, it happened: The Browser Company has finally announced that it will be sunsetting the Arc browser before the end of 2026. The writing has been on the wall for well over a year now: Arc had already been put on ice, receiving only maintenance updates after the Browser Company switched its focus to Dia, an AI browser that shares Arc’s framework but lacks the wonderful interface features that made Arc such a joy to use.

This is sad news for the Arc faithful. If you're one of them, or if you’re looking for an alternative to the regular browsers like Safari and Chrome, all hope is not lost. Export your Arc data, and try out one of these Arc-like alternatives.

Zen has become the de facto option for all users looking to find something that looks and works like Arc. In some ways, it’s better than Arc; in some ways it falls short.

I’ve been using Zen for months, and I’m quite happy with it. The only downside I can see is the Firefox web engine; while Gecko has come a long way, it can still sometimes fall short of Chromium, mostly because Google Chrome is such a popular browser, most websites are designed to run best on it. When I run into an issue with a website, I tend to switch to Chrome for a while. Zen can also sometimes be a memory hog, but once I got better at tab hygiene (automatically closing older tabs and being vigilant about workspace management), the experience got quite a bit better.

And yes, there is extension support: Anything that runs on Firefox will run here too. Firefox has most of the important extensions covered, and it’s the only major browser that still supports the full-scale uBlock Origin ad blocker (which works like a treat in Zen, too).

Alternatively, you can go to the opposite end of the spectrum and try out a maximalist browsing approac:. For a while, Microsoft Edge was the cleaner, faster, better version of Chrome, but now, that title goes to Vivaldi. Under the hood, Vivaldi uses the same Chromium engine that powers Google Chrome, so all your websites will work as expected, and all the extensions will be familiar. But Vivaldi is an extremely customizable browser, and for a certain kind of user, it might be the perfect fit.

There are tons of built-in features. It comes with an ad blocker and integrates with ProtonVPN for free, limited VPN access. You can add a free reader, email accounts, note-taking, and a calendar to the sidebar. Using the Web Panels feature, you can dock any website to the sidebar as well (this works well for media and messaging sites).

Vivaldi also has robust tab management features: You can use two websites in split screen (like with Zen and Arc), and you can organize tabs in workspaces. You can also group related tabs in Tab Stacks, Vivaldi’s unique two-level tab management system. One thing Vivaldi lacks by default is a vertical sidebar, which even Firefox and Chrome now support, though it can be added using a mod.

If you want to keep to a Chromium-based browser, but one that offers all the customization features you can think of, go for Vivaldi. At its core is a powerful, fast, and reliable browser that you can slowly remake to be your own.

Helium: Think of it as a minimalist version of Google Chrome. Same Chromium engine, but no Google tracker, no popups, ads, or extra features.

Dia: If you really want to use something that’s built by the same team as Arc, and don’t mind the AI features, you can try the Dia browser as well. It’s not an exact replacement, but Dia now has an option to use a vertical sidebar and pinned apps.

Quiche: If you were using Arc on iPhone or iPad, try using the Quiche browser, which is our favorite browser for the iPhone. It’s a tastefully designed independent browser, with a fully customizable layout.

#3614. GTA 6 PS5 Pro Features, Frame Rates, And Xbox Cloud Gaming Details Confirmed By Rockstar

Rockstar has finally shared details on what PlayStation 5 Pro owners can expect from Grand Theft Auto 6 on their expensive consoles, but has also confirmed that all platforms will run at the exact same frame rate.

PlayStation 5 Pro players can look forward to PSSR support, which will use Sony's well-tuned upscaler to provide a cleaner image compared to that on the base PS5. Additionally, ray-traced shadows will be exclusive to the PS5 Pro version, which might make a noticeable difference across Leonida depending on the time of day.

All of this will run at 30 frames per second across all platforms, Rockstar confirmed, with no mention of additional performance modes. Recent datamines suggested that GTA 6 might have numerous performance modes and additional frame rate support, but that doesn't seem to be the case yet.

In addition to PS5 Pro support, Rockstar has also announced that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming at launch. This means you won't need an Xbox Series X|S or PlayStation 5 to play arguably the biggest game of the year, with the Xbox One also supported via streaming exclusively. Cloud streaming won't be available on PlayStation consoles, but remote play (streaming from a console in your home) is supported on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is available to pre-load now across all release platforms, with some already reporting that GTA 6's story is appearing as a separate download, fuelling speculation that a new online mode isn't that far away. Recent reports have already suggested that a PC version for GTA 6 might launch in early 2027, which would be a much shorter turnaround time than previous Rockstar ports.

#3612. Benito Skinner’s ‘Overcompensating’ Returns for Season 2: More Laughs, More Sex, More Gay

It’s been a year and a half since the first season of Benito Skinner’s Prime Video comedy series, Overcompensating, debuted, and a lot has changed for him in that time. For one, Skinner—also known as Benny Drama, his online alter ego—is blond now. It’s a change he says may be permanent or perhaps semipermanent. “It’s how I see myself—as a blond,” he tells me over Zoom. “So we’re going to keep going with it for a sec.”

But Skinner has transformed in much less superficial ways since the launch of his hit Amazon series, which is based on his experiences coming out as gay as a Georgetown undergrad. Equal parts raunchy and heartwarming, the first season follows Benny (Skinner), a closeted former high school football player who attempts to navigate the chaos of college, where he forms an unlikely bond with a fellow student named Carmen (Wally Baram).

Skinner shares that making the second installment of the series was “way more fluid, way less stressed.” As it should have been. The first season was a popular hit for the streamer (it has a 93% fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes), hard-launching Skinner as an exciting new voice plucked from the internet and ready for prime time.

Benny and Carmen begin the season as enemies.

The second season, which Vanity Fair can exclusively reveal will debut on February 17, 2027, expands the world he created with new storylines for the supporting characters—and bigger stakes for Benny as he comes into his own with his sexuality. Benny navigates not only coming out to his sister, Grace (Mary Beth Barone), and his parents (Connie Britton and Kyle MacLachlan), but also his own sexual exploration—and all the awkwardness that comes with it.

So much of what made the first season a hit—the awkward comedy, the silly themed parties, the talking Megan Fox poster—returns, but this time many of the characters grapple with deeper issues. Yet Skinner felt lighter making the show this time around. “I think in season one, Benny is that stressed, so that kind of worked,” he says. “But in this one, we’re having more fun. He has some joy, so we can loosen up a little bit.”

Connie Britton, center, reprises her role as Benny's mom.

After Overcompensating premiered, Skinner was approached, he says, by “a few gays” who told him, “I thought it’d be gayer, the show.” He promises that the second season delivers just that: “We’re creeping out of the closet,” says Skinner.

In the first season, Benny is trying to find his place on campus while constantly living in fear that the people around him will discover he’s gay. He falls for a dashing British classmate named Miles (Rish Shah), only to find out he is straight and has kissed Carmen. The season ends with Carmen revealing that she has also slept with Grace’s boyfriend, Peter (Adam DiMarco), and in the final moments, Carmen accidentally lets slip in front of Grace that Benny is gay.

Skinner and Lukas Gage reunite in season two.

In the upcoming season, Benny heads back home with his sister for the start of Christmas break, struggling because he hasn’t yet come out to his family. “If season one was about friends, I think this season is about family, and trying to reintroduce yourself to your parents after starting to become yourself,” says Skinner. The way his father finds out about it makes for an especially tense moment, and Benny goes to great lengths (like joining the crew team) to mend that bond with his dad. “That relationship between gay men and father, I think, is always fraught and confusing,” he says. “I just wanted to make it as honest as possible.”

At the start of the new season, Benny and Carmen are at odds; Grace and her boyfriend, Peter, have broken up; and many of the characters are exploring those feelings of loneliness that can crop up in college. A handful of exciting new faces also join this season. Australian actor Aisha Dee (The Bold Type) plays a new student who becomes an instant It girl on campus. AnnaSophia Robb (The Carrie Diaries) joins as an intense coxswain (the one who does the yelling) on the crew team. And Tony-nominated stage actor Tom Francis (Sunset Boulevard) plays the captain of the team, serving as Benny’s newest love interest.

Peter (Adam DiMarco) is looking for his path forward.

For Skinner, the second season is about capturing the ups and downs of coming out. It’s not just one reveal and then you’re out of the closet and everything is better. “I get to be even more specific about coming out and also tell a story that I think I haven’t seen yet done in this way, which is the complication of coming out—how you can take 10 steps forward, a hundred steps back,” he says.

Benny joins the crew team, where he meets a new love interest (Tom Francis).

There’s also a lot more sex. “There are a couple scenes that are definitely going to be off-limits for the family,” Skinner says. But of course, in Overcompensating, the sex scenes aren’t always smooth sailing. “I think our show is about trying to be sexy and then it going wrong, or feeling like you start to come into yourself but you get made a fool,” he says.

Skinner adds the title of executive music producer to his résumé this season. “It feels like a return to my radio-DJ roots, and that feels right,” he says. There’s more Britney Spears and Charli xcx (who appeared in a cameo last season), and he wanted the show’s music to remain an important part of the world. He even wrote a letter to Coldplay when he wanted to use the band’s song “Fix You” in this new season. “I love doing the letters to these guys because I’m like, So is Chris Martin reading this? Is this sent by owl? What’s the vibe?” he says with a smile.

Overcompensating’s return will come almost two years after its debut, and Skinner, who says he always plans to keep this story set in the characters’ college years, wants to make the wait a little shorter next time. “I apologize to everyone that it took a while,” he says. “TV takes a long time, so I’m trying to go faster, but daddy has to write it.”

“I don’t want any of these characters to feel like we’re pandering to maybe what we think the internet will want,” says Skinner of crafting the second installment after a hit first season.

“What I wanted to do is surprise people with where we took it,” says Skinner of the new season, “and have them be like, ‘Oh, this isn’t what I asked for, but it is something kind of delicious and new.’”

#3611. Here’s How Your Xbox One Can Play GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto 6 is out next week, and the game is launching on both Xbox Series X|S and PS5. If you don't have an expensive current-generation system, it previously appeared you would be out of luck to play GTA 6, but that's not the case.

Rockstar officially confirmed on November 10 that Grand Theft Auto 6 will support Xbox Cloud Gaming. This feature allows you to stream the game to Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One, and uses Xbox Series S graphics settings. This means it'll look a little worse than running it natively on the Xbox Series X, but if you are still rocking with an Xbox One, this is the only way you can play the game.

"And as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay," Rockstar added in its announcement.

The catch to all this, outside of the game unlocking an hour later than the native versions, is that Microsoft just so happened to add a time limit to Xbox Cloud Gaming starting in November. If you have a Game Pass Ultimate subscription, you can play 15 hours a month via Xbox Cloud Gaming. Those without a subscription can buy time, as well, but 50 hours will cost $12, and that's on top of the cost of Grand Theft Auto 6 itself.

GTA 6 officially launches November 19. It will also support Remote Play across both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and includes some bonus performance features for PS5 Pro. Though the game will be single-player at launch, some files seem to suggest multiplayer is on the way.

#3610. The Newest Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition Is Finally Worth the Extra Money

I love e-readers, but I'd be the first to admit that as far as the general public is concerned, they are just about the least exciting tech devices around—and that goes double for the Amazon Kindle. Any attention the space has gotten over the past couple of years has involved obscure players like Boox and weird concepts like the phone-shaped Palma or the tiny Boox Picco. But the clear leader in terms of market share is still Amazon, and despite some minor innovations over the years, the device hasn't received an essential upgrade in around a decade: A Kindle is a Kindle is a Kindle.

I'd still say this holds true in 2026, even after the company unveiled a complete redesign of the Kindle lineup (this, a few months after significantly raising prices across all of the devices). While the new flush-front display is nice-looking (and Amazon is quite proud of the new process it has developed to add colored bezels by painting them directly onto the outer glass screen), competitors have offered similar designs for years, and it's hard to get too excited about "innovations" like an $80 case that adds back the physical buttons that used to be built in or finally opening up the firmware to allow for the use of a Bluetooth page-turn remote.

But one thing has changed about the 2026 Kindle lineup: I think the $50 premium Amazon charges for the top-of-the-line Signature Editions of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft is finally truly justified.

Amazon introduced the first "Signature Edition" of the Kindle Paperwhite back in 2021, and while the 25% price increase didn't get you nothing, the features it did add weren't too exciting: At 32GB, it had three times the storage versus the standard Paperwhite, but how important is a ton of storage when most e-book files are tiny? (That's still enough room for more than 6,000 texts, well more than even true bookworms will read in an entire lifetime.) Other bonuses, like wireless charging and an auto-adjusting front light, won't matter at all to a huge subset of readers, and it's hard to think of "no ads on the lock screen" as an extra perk.

But the latest Signature Editions of the Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft actually give you more for the price premium, and for the first time, I would recommend shelling out the extra cash. While the important specs are still the same as the standard model:

7-inch, 300ppi flush-front display (with color content on the Colorsoft maxing out at 150ppi)

USB-C charging with battery life "up to 12 weeks on a single charge," per Amazon

Bluetooth support for wireless headphones

...the Signature Editions give you quite a bit more this time around, including, most noticeably, a totally new design with an all-metal rear panel that gives the devices a much sleeker look and feel without adding much in the way of weight (the standard plastic models weigh around 7.2 ounces, while the Signature Editions weigh 8.1 ounces). The new design makes the Signature Editions feel truly premium.

But that's not the only meaningful addition. Once again, alongside wireless charging and automatically adjusting lighting, the Signature Editions have a boosted 32GB of storage, which is still probably overkill, but worthwhile if you like to load your device with a bunch of audiobooks or (in the case of the Colorsoft) color comics.

You also get an accelerometer, which means the display will auto-rotate if you flip it upside down, giving you more flexibility in how you hold it (especially if you're springing for the new Page-Turn Cover, which brings back physical buttons à la the beloved, discontinued Kindle Oasis). Moreover, there's a new ability to turn pages by double-tapping on the bottom sides or back of the device rather than touching the screen (though it only works for moving forward in your book).

Speaking of which, you'll need to go for the Signature Editions if you want to use accessories like the Page-Turn Cover or the also-new Charging Stand (not yet available for pre-order), as only the Signature Editions include the built-in magnetic pogo pins you'll need to connect them. (If you're interested in the Kindle Click page-turn remote, it at least works with any Kindle from 2024 or later.)

Finally, if you care about your Kindle looking pretty, it's worth noting that only the Signature Editions are available in Seaglass Green (for the Paperwhite) and the reddish-purple Plum (for the Colorsoft).

Outside of those extras, the 2026 Kindles don't feel much different than the 2024 models. According to Amazon, they are the fastest Kindles ever, but that's mostly hype—any recent Kindle will turn pages quickly enough that you'll barely notice the speed difference, if you notice it at all. They all still run on the same firmware, which is both a good thing (Amazon makes it extremely easy to browse for and buy books and audiobooks directly on the device; there are a ton of options to search through and sort your library; and quality-of-life features like being able to sideload books via email using the "Send to Kindle" feature are a godsend) and a bad thing (I hope you like being locked into the Amazon ecosystem).

One change to the entire 2026 Kindle lineup is already proving divisive: Judging by reactions on the Kindle Reddit, not everyone is in love with the new flush-front design, which eliminates the raised bezels around the screen that were present on the 2024 model, but at the cost of adding a thin layer of glass over the e-ink display.Depending on how picky you are, you may find fault with this setup, as the additional layer of glass slightly reduces text clarity by putting more distance and another barrier between your eyes and the text or images in your book. Is this something I noticed myself? No—I don't have an older Kindle to make a direct comparison, and the text is still much, much sharper (and the front lighting more even) than what I see on competing e-readers like the Boox Go 6 or the Xteink X4 Pro. But there is a contingent of readers already lamenting the change, so take that for what you will.

The question to consider whenever a new device model rolls around is simple: Is this worth the upgrade? If you have a working Kindle from any time after the introduction of temperature-adjustable lighting, I would say no—the 2026 models are nicer, but they still don't do anything to make them worth it, especially at the new higher price points. That said, if you are in the market for a new Kindle, I'd suggest opting for the Paperwhite over the entry-level model, which has a smaller screen and lacks the warm light option—and if you're getting a Paperwhite or Colorsoft, you might as well pay the premium for the Signature Edition, because it's finally worth the extra money.

Andrei and Libby Castravet have spent years entertaining 90 Day Fiancé fans with their up-and-down relationship. However, it would seem those days are now over. After missing out on appearing on the 2026 TV schedule, the couple have announced that they're leaving the franchise. And, with that, they're not mincing words about the situation.

While Libby soft-launched the departure with some posts on Instagram, Andrei was a bit more explicit. He popped up in the comments and shared a goodbye in a way only he could. For better or worse, this departure is unapologetically filled with Andrei's signature attitude (via John Yates):

For the imbeciles that watched for 10 years and were not entertained for what I bring to the table, suck it. Go color your hair pink and go protest lol. The other majority who understands what I was doing, I appreciate youuuu. I said it during the summer time before they started this new HEA, I'm not doing trash TV anymore. They don't pay enough. The best decision ever, watch what happens next. New project coming!

This situation marks just the latest instance in which a high-profile couple to depart the 90 Day Fiancé series. And only months ago, Shekinah Güven also vowed she'd never work with 90 Day again. It sounds like Libby and Andrei, at the very least, may have something lined up, though they haven't dropped any clues as to what that might be.

I'm Shocked By How Much 90 Day Fiancé's Sarper Reportedly Made Doing Stand-Up Comedy

Libby and Andrei leaving 90 Day Fiancé comes a year after the unexpected passing of her father and fellow 90 Day star, Chuck Potthast. She wrote about dealing with grief following his passing, and perhaps shutting the door on this chapter is a way for the couple to move on.

Their time in 90 Day was not peaceful and created major rifts in their family. Libby became estranged from her brother, Charlie, as well as her sisters, as they took issue with Andrei's brash attitude and the way he fit into their way of life.

As for what comes next, I could imagine they're hoping to get involved in a show that plays to his skills as a real estate agent. HGTV still has plenty of shows with which they could make that transition, assuming there's a casting agent out there willing to give the couple a shot.

Still, if I had a nickel for every time a 90 Day Fiancé star said they were leaving to do bigger and better things, I'd have a ton of nickels. Ultimately, many of these people leave and end up struggling to find another series to appear on. Angela Deem may be the most notable case of this, having gone from one of the franchise's biggest stars to being absent from TV. She's recently hinted that her comeback is coming, but no concrete details have been shared on that front, as of this writing.

It's worth noting that other 90 Day Fiancé fans aren't buying the Andrei & Libby news and feel that the couple will eventually appear in a future season of The Last Resort. I'm skeptical of that, but I can add that, of all the deception we've seen from 90 Day stars over the years about their true plans, Libby and her family are pros at keeping fans in the dark. For now, we can only wait to see what happens.

#3607. Kylie Jenner Sued by Another Housekeeper Who Was Allegedly Locked in Closet

Kylie Jenner and members of her team are facing a lawsuit filed by a former housekeeper who alleges she was locked inside the star’s closet, bitten by a dog and struck in the eyes with pepper spray while on the job.

Court documents filed with the Superior Court of California on Thursday, November 5, and obtained by Us on Tuesday, November 10, state that Dinora Carolina Cabria Amaya is claiming that Jenner, 29, her staff supervisor Laura Dooley and other team members were responsible for her being locked inside Jenner’s closet “for more than one hour” before being “mocked” when asked to exit and experiencing a panic attack while kept inside.

The documents also detail Amaya’s claims that she was bitten by a dog on October 28, 2025, after being asked to clean the animal’s “doghouse.” She also detailed an alleged September 4, 2025 incident that involved her “cleaning and organizing a drawer in the laundry room [when] an unsecured canister of pepper spray discharged directly into” Amaya’s eyes and face.

Us has reached out to a representative for Jenner for comment.

Amaya, who states that she was paid $40 per hour from March 2025, is also alleging that she was wrongfully terminated on February 6 due to her “protected wage-related complaints” and “workplace treatment.”

In an additional claim, Amaya alleged that “she was constantly asked to set up a massage table for Jenner in the glam room or lift heavy 13-gallon trash bags to throw away.”

Amaya is seeking compensation from Jenner and her team for “lost earnings, lost employment benefits, emotional distress, humiliation, anxiety, and other damages according to proof,” with no numerical figure specified.

The filing is the fourth lawsuit lodged against Jenner and her team since April 17 when another former housekeeper Angelica Hernandez Vasquez claimed that she was harassed and discriminated against while working for the cosmetics queen.

The following month, Jenner was sued by a further part-time housekeeper, Juana Delgado Soto, who alleged that she experienced racial harassment and racial discrimination while employed by her team.

One month after that, a former private chef filed a lawsuit alleging pregnancy discrimination, wrongful termination and workplace strain.

Jenner has not publicly addressed any of the lawsuits, however her attorney Michael Rhodes told TMZ on Tuesday that each case is being filed by a single lawyer. “These latest cases are being brought by the same lawyer who previously filed claims on behalf of Kylie’s former household staff,” the statement read.“It’s clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday.”

It concluded, “We’re not going to be intimidated into doing that. As such, we’ll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story.”

Amaya’s lawsuit includes 21 individual complaints that extend beyond her allegations of physical strain including failure to pay minimum wages, failure to pay overtime compensation, failure to provide meal periods, failure to authorize and permit rest periods and failure to pay all wages due upon termination.

#3606. Sony Is Bringing The Best Trend Of ’90s Console Design To PS5

Sony is embracing one of the best trends of the late '90s and early 2000s, revealing a new line of DualSense controllers and PlayStation 5 console covers with transparent materials. Dubbed the Prism Collection, it will come in three distinct glossy colors: Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray.  Preorders will open on November 10 through the PlayStation Direct store ahead of a February 4, 2027 rollout.

Sony says the design was inspired by the PS5 design team's interest in giving the console and its accessories a transparent look while also showing off the hardware beneath the protective surface. Flare Orange has a "bold and vibrant aesthetic," Emerald Green offers an "elegant" finish, and Sony says a PS5 will look "refined" with a Graphite Gray cover.

"We know how much our fans have been looking forward to the return of transparent controllers," Leo Cardoso and Satoshi Aoyagi from Sony's Color, Material, and Finish design team said in a press statement. "We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5's industrial design. "The high-gloss clear finish extends across the back of the controller, offering a look at the technology that powers the DualSense controller while maintaining a sleek, monochromatic look. The metallic finish on the middle cover brings the contrasting surfaces together for a premium appearance that feels consistent with the PS5 generation."

The Prism Collection DualSense controllers have an MSRP of $85 each, while the PS5 console covers are priced at $75 each. If you missed it, Sony also launched limited-edition Marathon and Gran Turismo DualSense controllers this year, and Marvel's Wolverine fans can grab a new PS5 console cover and matching DualSense controller in striking yellow or adamantium-inspired silver, complete with claw marks.

There are a lot of upcoming Hallmark movies to look forward to, especially as Countdown to Christmas continues. Many of these films are led by Hallmark staples, of course, but it’s hard not to think about previous network stars who used to headline those offerings. This includes Danica McKellar, who is one of many ex-Hallmark stars to have joined rival company GAF. However, the Wonder Years alum is speaking out about the whole situation and wants fans to know she didn’t leave.

In 2021, McKellar exited Hallmark after signing a multi-picture deal with Great American Family. Over her six-year tenure at Hallmark, McKellar starred in nearly 20 films, so it was definitely a shock when her departure was confirmed. However, McKellar recently clarified the situation and made note of how Bill Abbott -- the former president and CEO of Hallmark Channel’s parent company, Crown Media -- factored into it. She told PauseRewind via Komo News:

I don't feel like I left. I feel like I stayed with the person and he has just given me so much more creative freedom.

Abbott was the president and CEO of Crown Media for 11 years before ultimately starting GAF. Considering their prior working relationship, it's admittedly understandable that McKellar would want to follow him to a new network. And, of course, the desire for more creative freedom is also reasonable for an actor.

So, from McKellar's point of view, she didn’t “leave” Hallmark but simply stuck with the person who helped build the network amid his venture into something new. As for how her new work situation is going, McKellar notes that she’s much more involved at GAF when it comes to making her movies. Overall, it sounds like the former child star has been relishing that:

I’m involved in rewrites for sure on the script. I help casting. I help make decisions about props. Sometimes I buy my own wardrobe or props because I'm like, oh, this would be perfect and they're always so receptive, which is great. And I'm very involved in the edit, choosing music, all that kind of stuff.

McKellar’s feelings about having creative control and being more involved are similar to what Candace Cameron Bure has said about GAF. The Full House alum, who also made the switch from Hallmark in 2022, has opened up about living her dream making faith-centered movies. She serves as an executive producer on all of her GAF films and even some films she doesn’t appear in. It definitely seems like both McKellar and Bure are a lot more hands-on than they were at Hallmark.

Even though McKellar is no longer on the network, she has no problem defending her Hallmark movies either. They’ve gotten a bad rap over the years, with many pointing out that Hallmark movies are far too predictable and the network hasn’t embraced POC and LGBTQ+-centric stories. However, the cable channel has been working to make some changes over the years, and McKellar still shows her support to her Hallmark friends and their movies.

While I miss seeing Danica McKellar on her previous network, I can’t say I blame her for being content at Great American Family. It's my hope that she continues to headline entertaining films that delight audiences whether they arrive during the holidays or not. On that note, though, with the holiday season coming up, there are going to be a lot more Christmas movies to look forward to that aren’t just on Hallmark.
